items.statement: Operational portfolio of 2,890 MW capable of delivering annual steady-state project-level EBITDA of INR 2,000-2,050 crores with EBITDA yield of 14%-15%
items.quote: With this, our operational portfolio of independent power producers now stands at 2890 MW, capable of delivering an annual steady state project level EBITDA of INR2,000 to INR2,050 crores and an EBITDA yield of around 14%-15%.

items.statement: Under-construction portfolio stands at 4,080 MW plus 550 MWh storage; 55% of portfolio has signed PPAs
items.quote: Further, in this quarter, we signed PPAs of 550 MW of FDRE and solar project and 550 MWh are of standalone BESS projects. With this, our under construction portfolio stands at 4080 MW plus 550 MW h are of storage and 55% of our portfolio has signed PPAs.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is INR 12,000-14,000 crores; similar number expected for FY27; purchase orders of ~INR 7,000 crores already placed
items.quote: for this year we have guided around INR12,000 crores to INR 14,000 crores of capex. And of course for the next year also similar sort of number.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 91% aided by operational capacity growth and reduction in overall percentage cost
items.quote: We had a very healthy EBITDA margin which is aided by the operational capacity growth and also reduction in the overall percentage cost. So, the margin is now at 91%.

items.statement: Net operational debt to EBITDA at 4.2x, well within guided range of 5.5x; net debt to net worth at 1.7x
items.quote: we continue to maintain strong balance sheet discipline with net operational debt to EBITDA at 4.2x. How we calculate is basically the operational project debt and the operational project EBITDA. This is well within our guided range of 5.5x which we seek to maintain at all times.

items.statement: Days of sales outstanding dropped to 36 days in Q1; central off-takers proportion in portfolio moved to 86%
items.quote: Further, days of sales outstanding has dropped to 36 days in Q1. Of course, the proportion of central off -takers in our overall portfolio has moved to 86% now.

items.statement: Four SECI assets totalling 1,200 MW secured CRISIL AA- stable rating within six months of full operations
items.quote: On credit rating, we are pleased to share that within six months of full operations, our four SECI assets with a cumulative capacity of 1,200 megawatt have secured CRISIL AA - stable rating.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 generation of 163 crore units, up 107% YoY; capacity utilization factor improved to 28.5% from 27%
items.quote: In Q1 FY26, we generated 163 crore s units up over 107% year -on-year and our capacity utilization factor improved to 28.5% from 27% last year.

items.statement: Ministry of Power announced second tranche of VGF scheme with INR 5,400 crores outlay; VGF of INR 18 lakh per MWh to enable 30 GWh BESS capacity; ISTS waiver extended for co-located BESS till June 2028
items.quote: Ministry of Power announced the second tranche of VGF scheme with a total financial outlay of around INR5,400 crores. This aids the development of the BESS projects across states. VGF around 18 lakh per megawatt hour will be provided under this scheme which w ill enable development of 30 gigawatt hour of BESS capacity.

items.statement: India's overall power demand in Q1 FY26 stood at 446 billion units, reflecting ~1% YoY decline; peak demand at 242 GW, down 3.2% YoY; early monsoon and higher base cited
items.quote: India's overall power demand during Q1 FY26 stood at 446 billion units reflecting a 1% odd year-on-year decline. Similarly, peak power demand du ring the quarter stood at 242 gigawatt marking a 3.2% decline over the same period last year.

items.statement: Secured first standalone BESS project of 550 MWh with NHPC; signed PPAs for 550 MW FDRE/solar and 550 MWh standalone BESS; placed orders for 3.1 GWh BESS with Narada and Trina Energy
items.quote: In terms of new win s, we secured our first standalone battery energy storage projects of 550 MWh contracted with NHPC. The PPA was signed in a quick time of one month. This marks a major diversification into energy storage, pure energy storage contract.

items.statement: BESS capex at ~$100/kWh landed cost including BOS, transformer, duties and logistics; FDRE capex ~INR 11 cr/MW, hybrid ~INR 8 cr/MW
items.quote: So it is much less than that. And the IRR in this is of course lesser than the FDRE, but the risk is also much lesser than the FDRE. So they are in high-teens. So we don't do a project which is less than a 16% return. So the returns are much above that for this project.

items.statement: Targeting commissioning of 450 MW capacity and ~2.5 GWh battery component of FDRE projects in FY26; battery commissioning phased across Q3/Q4
items.quote: So just to conclude, w e would be adding 450 megawatt of capacity and around 2.5 gigawatt hours of battery component of the FDRE projects which we can generate revenue from.

items.statement: PPA signing pace picked up; 550 MW FDRE/solar and 550 MWh BESS signed in Q1; expect to conclude pipeline in 4 months; Omega Urja (252 MW) expected this month, SECI hybrid (325 MW) in August
items.quote: As you must have seen, 550 MW of FDRE and solar we have signed, and 550 MWh of battery we have signed. So pace has definitely picked up. And the various states are now off taking these powers.

items.statement: Portfolio interest cost ~8.75% on operating projects; expect significant reduction this FY due to COD reset, annual reset, refinancing and RBI rate cuts; 3 of 4 SECI projects yet to be refinanced
items.quote: our interest cost on a portfolio basis especially for operating projects is close to 8.75% as we speak. But, you know, we are in the process of refinancing a lot of this debt and also there is an interest cost reduction when the COD happens. So, I think during this financial year as we end this financial year we are expecting much significant reduction in the interest cost.

items.statement: Holding company rating A+ positive outlook; expect consistent AA family ratings for projects; exploring capital market funding (mutual funds, insurance, provident funds) for diversification and cost reduction
items.quote: Today our holding company rating is A+ with positive outlook. We look to taking it further as we keep on adding more and more projects. And so certain mix of this financing going forward could be from capital market, gives us diversification into various fund providers such as mutual funds, insurance companies and also provident funds.

items.statement: Importing full containerized BESS from global suppliers (Narada, Trina) to ensure warranty reliability; local assembly avoided at nascent stage; duty difference 5-11% but warranty risk outweighs savings
items.quote: Assembly at this time, when the industry at nascent stage, is not a very good strategy. It can happen later, right? The government is the -- that is the reason even the government has given the option that you can get the full battery from outside by payi ng a small duty while you are importing.

items.statement: Central off-takers proportion increased to 86% of portfolio; NHPC BESS project involves storing energy for Andhra Pradesh government; long-term service agreements with Narada and Trina for O&M
items.quote: Of course, the proportion of central off -takers in our overall portfolio has moved to 86% now. So, this really bodes well for cash flow generation for us.

items.statement: Early commissioning of BESS requires regulatory approvals (NOC from counterparties, NRLDC); wind resource variability risk minimized by reducing wind component in FDRE; land and transmission risks minimal for battery plants
items.quote: So the regulatory piece, it is new. So you need to take all these approvals which we are taking for the first time. So similarly, the procurement, again. But there are upsides to all of that. Because once you, your base case assumptions are getting bettered in most cases.

items.statement: Completed 5 years continuous testing of FDRE (battery, solar, grid); battery degradation well within limits; tested power electronics reliability on weak 33 kV grid; validated charging/discharging efficiency; testing perovskite technology a
items.quote: I would like to share with you that last week we finished five years of continuous testing of the FDRE, which is the battery, solar and the grid together. And we were able to test the battery degradation, and I'm very happy to share with you they were very well within the limit, what we have thought of, of five years of continuous testing.

items.statement: Capex financed 75:25 debt-equity; FY26 capex INR 14,000 cr implies ~INR 11,500 cr debt but weighted average debt addition much lower due to back-ended spend; using buyer's credit during LC phase to reduce construction period interest cost
items.quote: capex is financed 75-25 in terms of debt and equity for us. And typically what we have seen is post -capex, we get revenue within 8 to 9 months of that capex, weighted average capex being done. So in terms of this financial year, our capex target is close to, let's say, INR 14,000 crores, but it may -- but the weighted average, so the debt for that would be around INR 11,500 crores.

items.statement: 2.2 GW signed PPA capacity scheduled for commissioning by FY27, staggered across FY26/FY27; connectivity sourced pre-bid de-linking PPA signing from connectivity timelines; no major transmission delays seen
items.quote: So you're right, Mohit. That 2.2 gigawatt will be done by FY '27. And it is staggered across FY '26 and FY '27, the connectivity. So we are not seeing much delay. And the reason for that is we have sourced our connectivity independent of these bids.

items.statement: Early commissioning of BESS (pre-COD) to sell in merchant market at peak tariffs; 12-month avg peak tariff ~INR 9/kWh (1-hr) and INR 8.78/kWh (2-hr); charging cost lower; FDRE battery revenue potential substantially higher than NHPC BESS (I
items.quote: Typically, what we are seeing is around 9 hours is the peak tariff on a 1 hour average basis for the last 12 months and 8.78 is the average for 2 hours in the last 12 months. So, that is the reference number and the production cost you can see, this is the reference capex we have given.

items.statement: Standalone BESS project commissioning timeline 18 months (vs 24 months for FDRE); land and evacuation onus on customer; NHPC project can commission in 6 months once notice to proceed received
items.quote: Yes, yes, yes, yes. It is 18 months in... It depends on the size of the project but the project we have won is 18 months and the onus on giving the land and the evacuation lies on the customer.

items.statement: BESS tendering slowed last quarter but picking up with multiple bids from REIAs; trend shifted to solar+storage and pure storage; 30 GWh VGF announced to be consumed by states this year/next; 24-hour procurement tenders expected to drive hi
items.quote: The trend has shifted to solar plus storage and pure storage. So we are seeing less of and hopefully the 24-hour, the whole day procurement will also pick up that, because that will really lead to a higher growth of the peak power in the country. So we see that this growth will be very high. It will be much higher than the last year is what we feel.

items.statement: CDSL opened 56 lakh Demat accounts in Q1 FY26, total 15.86 crore accounts, 79% market share as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: CDSL saw more than 56 lakh accounts open ed in this quarter, bringing our total to 15.86 crore Demat accounts, maintaining a 79% market share. This is as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Industry average daily turnover at BSE & NSE was INR 1.16 lakh crores in Q1 FY26, up 15% from previous quarter
items.quote: The average daily turnover at BS E & NSE in Q1 FY '26 was at about INR1.16 lakh crores, a jump of 15% from the last quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated total income INR 295 crores, net profit INR 102 crores for quarter ended June 2025
items.quote: Speaking on the consolidated quarterly performance, the total income for the quarter ended June 2025 is achieved at INR295 crores as against INR287 crores for the previous corresponding quarter. The net profit for the quarter ended June 2025 is at INR102 crores as against INR134 crores for the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Standalone total income INR 312 crores, net profit INR 152 crores for quarter ended June 2025
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, the total income for the quarter ended June 2025 is at INR312 crores as against INR221 crores for the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The net profit for the quarter June 2025 is at INR152 crores as against INR105 crores for the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: CDSL Ventures total income INR 43.06 crores, profit after tax INR 12.71 crores for three-month FY26
items.quote: CVL total income for the three -month FY '26 was at INR43.06 crores as compared to INR64.37 crores for three-month FY '25. The total expenditure was at INR30.35 crores for three -month FY '26 as against INR35.82 crores for three -month FY '25. The profit after tax for three-months FY26 was at INR12.71 crores as against INR28.55 crores.

items.statement: Average folio count for FY26 is INR 33.26 crores, up from INR 22.76 crores previous period
items.quote: So, the folio, average folio for this financial year is INR33.26 crores.

items.statement: KYC revenue is around 13% of total consolidated revenue in current quarter
items.quote: It is around 13% in the current quarter.

items.statement: Other income breakup: CAS INR 13 crores, e-voting INR 6.5 crores, investment income INR 35 crores, e-sign/e-KYC INR 4.5 crores, miscellaneous INR 7 crores
items.quote: the income from consolidated account statement is at INR13 crores, e-voting at INR6.5 crores. The other part of other income which has been reported in the investor presentation is largely on account of the investment income which is at INR35 crores. Apart from that, we have e-sign and e-KYC income of INR4.5 crores and miscellaneous income of INR7 crores.

items.statement: Technology spend across infrastructure, application, security, network for new products and platform enhancement; continuous evolution expected
items.quote: On the technology front, on all the four components of infrastructure, application, security and network is where we are continuously innovating as per the new products which are getting initiated. This is to bring in a lot of nimbleness in our systems but at the same time bring in the best-in-class products.

items.statement: SEBI depository regulations require focus on vertical 1 (IT/critical ops), vertical 2 (risk/control), vertical 3 (business); CDSL building long-term resilient infrastructure
items.quote: For depositories, there is a separate regulation and separate for exchanges and clearing corporation. It constitutes into vertical 1, vertical 2 and vertical 3, where the IT and critical operations form a part of vertical 1, regulation risk and control functions form part of vertical 2 and business and others form part of vertical 3.

items.statement: CKYC revamp from March 2026; KRAs to integrate with CKYC; early days but existing system benefits expected to continue
items.quote: Yes, like just what Nehal said, the KRAs will be integrating with the CKYC. That is all we know about it as of now. So, as and when it happens, and we have more details, we will be able to tell you how it is going to happen.

items.statement: Transaction charges INR 3.50 (INR 0.50 cheaper than competition); INR 0.25 discount for female investors, mutual funds, bonds; issuer charges need regulator approval
items.quote: So, the price for issue for the investors or transaction was that that one charge with the circular requires. So that time we had factored in certain economies of scale and made it at 3.5. We are about INR0.50 cheaper than our competition. This is to factor in the economies of scale. And there was an additional INR0.25 discount given for female investors in the first to encourage a lot of diversit

items.statement: Issuer charges increase is continuous process with regulator; confidentiality maintained on discussions with SEBI
items.quote: Issuer charges has been increasing on a periodic basis. As you know, depository charges have to be approved by the regulator. So, this is something which is a continuous process of work in progress and as we factor in. So, as and when the necessary approvals come in, it is, I would be able to disclose it only once it comes out in the public domain.

items.statement: 3-in-1 account technology APIs and solutions in place; CDSL facilitates Demat side, bank partnerships handled by DPs
items.quote: We have the necessary technology APIs and solutions for them to kind of factor that in. It's a bank account versus Demat account. So, we are responsible as a depository for the Demat account and ensuring that the necessary technology enablement's are already in place.

items.statement: Unlisted space: 3,486 companies admitted in Q1 FY26; total outstanding ~20,000+ companies
items.quote: this quarter, we have admitted 3,486 companies in unlisted space. Devesh Agarwal: In all, sir? Outstanding number as on date? Girish Amesara: I don't have that number ready, but it would be in the range of 20,000 plus

items.statement: Demat accounts with zero holdings percentage stable over last 2-3 years; no significant increase
items.quote: No. It's more or less remaining at the same constant percentage. But again, see, people have holdings, then they sell off those holdings, so they become zero. Then again, it's a constantly dynamic concept.

items.statement: Demat market share gain from centralized architecture, lower infra cost, technology platform, service standards; issuer side historically restricted ISIN issuance to one depository
items.quote: It has been, it is a culmination of technology platform service standards . So , from an infra standpoint, we are a centralized architecture from a cost of holding that infra is lower. There is a variety of measures which has caused this advantage too. On the private limited, it is a process , and we are continuously working towards that why they have been chosen. Only one reason which I can say t

items.statement: EBITDA margin not a target; byproduct of providing right platform; technology expense constant evolution like road maintenance
items.quote: Our intent is to provide a long-term proposition. Whatever EBITDA we earn, our intent is not to earn a particular EBITDA margin, either high or low. We ensure that the right platform is provided to the market, to the ecosystem. EBITDA margin is the byproduct of that because I think it's the intent is the long-term intent to ensure that the value proposition continues to be enjoyed by the ecosystem

items.statement: Technology expense constant evolution; no plateau; continuous investment as accounts grow and new tech emerges
items.quote: I don't think it is basically a start and stop kind of technology expense. It's a constant process of evolution as we embark on a journey. And therefore, there will be a constantly a process of evolving this thing. It is like saying your roads, you have a particular road and you build another road as the traffic grows. Again, you keep on maintaining that road with better material. So, better techn

items.statement: Higher consolidated tax rate due to dividend from subsidiaries; deferred tax portion increases at consolidated level
items.quote: See Amit, normally we receive dividends from our subsidiary companies. And that we take advantage for the purpose of taxation on a stand-alone basis. So, when we do a consolidation in the first quarter, wherever there is a dividend increase in stand -alone, the tax, deferred portion of the tax tends to increase at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Sequential demand uptick in Q1 FY26 across T1-T4 cities; early monsoons in June dampened coatings demand but urban green shoots seen
items.quote: we saw a slight uptick in demand sequentially and both T1, T2 cities and T3, T4 cities, we were seeing almost equal demand conditions.

items.statement: July demand similar to Q1 pattern; Q3 may be affected by fewer retail days due to early Diwali
items.quote: we have seen a little bit of a similar pattern in July as well as we have been seeing in Q1 in terms of demand.

items.statement: India decorative volume grew 3.9% YoY in Q1 FY26 on a 7.1% base; value declined 1.2%
items.quote: Overall, the volume growth has been decent. We've got about 3.9% volume growth over the Q1 of last year, which was also at about 7 .1% volume growth.

items.statement: Overall coatings volume grew 4.2% YoY; value flat YoY; industrial coatings grew 8.8%
items.quote: When we look at putting the industrial numbers along with this. So, look at the overall coatings piece, the volume goes to about 4.2% and the value is just at about the base of what we see.

items.statement: Economy emulsions, waterproofing (Smart Care), exterior textures, wood finishes did well; luxury emulsions saw downtrading
items.quote: economy emulsions has done well. The waterproofing business, which is under the brand Smart Care is something which is another one which did well. Exterior textures, wood finishes, these were areas which have done quite well.

items.statement: New products contributed 14% of overall revenue in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This quarter we saw about 14% contribution coming to the overall revenues from the new products.

items.statement: Committed ~700 crore capex for FY26; ~100 crore spent in Q1; white cement plant near commissioning; VAM/VAE plant benefits from Q1 FY27
items.quote: we have committed closer to 700 crores of CapEx this year. We've spent about 100 crores this year already on that.

items.statement: White cement plant in Dubai near commissioning; VAM/VAE emulsion plant in Dahej on track for Q1 FY27 benefits
items.quote: our white cement plant is near commissioning. So, we should start soon seeing the benefits of the white cement outputs to start coming in the next quarters or so.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 43.2% in Q1 FY26 (+40 bps YoY); PBDIT 19.4% (down YoY, up QoQ); consolidated gross 42.6%, PBDIT 18.2%
items.quote: Gross margins as I just said is 43.2, a little bit higher than Q1 of last year, but by and large strong PBDIT margins again is still healthy at 19.4%.

items.statement: Raw material deflation ~1% in Q1; TiO2 anti-dumping duty to add 1.5-2.5% to raw material cost index; pricing decision pending
items.quote: the overall deflation is what we have seen this quarter is closer to 1%.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on TiO2 from China will increase raw material cost index by 1.5-2.5%; Chinese suppliers have lowered prices but not enough to offset duty
items.quote: From the point of impact of ADD alone, the impact would be anywhere from 1.5% to 2.5% in the overall raw material cost index level.

items.statement: Maintains PBDIT margin guidance of 18-20% despite cost pressures; focusing on cost excellence, formulation and sourcing efficiencies
items.quote: So, as of now, we will keep the guidance on in terms of our 18 to 20% guidance.

items.statement: Near-term growth outlook: single-digit volume and value growth given current demand conditions
items.quote: We are still looking at basically a single digit growth in how it would pan out in overall numbers in terms of both value and volume as we go ahead.

items.statement: Competition intense from new and existing players; new entrant's 10% extra grammage viewed as intermediary discount not consumer proposition
items.quote: So, I think that according to us will not really matter too much in this thing you have seen almost a year plus, that thing going in the market, and we see it as a discount in what possibly the new competition is giving.

items.statement: Distribution footprint ~1.7 lakh retail outlets; painting services growing with strong NPS; 72 Beautiful Home stores; Nilaya Anthology design center launched
items.quote: Our whole painting service is something which is going strong. We have a strong NPS which comes in and we have a large footprint now across the country where we are able to offer these services.

items.statement: Industrial business (PPG-AP) grew 11% with healthy PBT margins; APPPG grew 5% with margin pressure from competitive pricing
items.quote: the PPGAP business which talks of auto refinishes, industrial marine business. This business has done quite well with double-digit growth, 11% is the growth what we have registered.

items.statement: International business (AP Global) grew 8.4% in INR terms, 17.5% in constant currency; strong in Sri Lanka, Nepal, UAE, Egypt; Ethiopia hit by currency
items.quote: Overall, we got a strong global presence. We grew almost 8.4% in INR terms. In constant currency growth would be closer to 17.5%.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty imposed on TiO2 imports from China; impact to start in Q2 FY26
items.quote: in the paint industry we also have anti-dumping duty which is being imposed in key raw material which is TiO 2.

items.statement: Higher rebates/sales & marketing spend in Q1 to drive sustainable growth; not a short-term discounting strategy
items.quote: overall, you know we have upped our sales and marketing expenses the way we have gone in the market. Because as I said very clearly, we are looking at growth as we go ahead

items.statement: IT sector job cuts could impact new construction demand; luxury segment downtrading observed; monsoon intensity risk for Q3 retail days
items.quote: However, what we see very clearly is when we look at from a point of view of demand, our demand is divided into two, three kinds of segments.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on innovation, regionalization, and brand saliency to drive growth
items.quote: what we are channelizing in terms of our ways is very clear that as we go ahead, we will look at possibly very strong ways to keep on growing, looking at innovation, brand saliency, looking at very different ways of what we can look at various regions

items.statement: FY26 standalone revenue guidance INR8,000-8,500 crore, EBITDA margin ~11%, order inflow INR12,000-15,000 crore, capex INR40-50 crore
items.quote: The guidance, what we expect should be in the range of INR8,000 crores to INR8,500 crores of revenue and this is for the full year. And the EBITDA margin should be in the range of 11% or so.

items.statement: Expect INR12,000-15,000 crore new order inflow in FY26, with major momentum in Q3-Q4
items.quote: At least we are expecting INR12,000 crores to INR15,000 crores of new order inflow. So that is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Standalone capex negligible at INR40-50 crore for FY26, only replacement capex
items.quote: It should be very negligible if only some replacement capex has to be done. So I don't expect to be more than -- if at all, because we are expecting it not to go, but let's -- for assumption sake, let's assume between INR 40 to 50 crores.

items.statement: Standalone debt reduction target INR500 crore by March 2026 intact, net debt free by FY27 intact
items.quote: So basically, our target for 31st March 2026, the reduction of debt by INR500 crores remains intact, number one. Number two, it is a quarterly increase by INR85 crores, which we will address in 9 months. So there are activities quarters. So the plan is intact.

items.statement: Consol net debt INR8,266 crore as of June 2025; INR3,850 crore to move to InvIT, net reduction ~INR3,000 crore by March 2026
items.quote: So let me tell you on quarter 1 ending, my net debt is INR8,266 crores. Basically, out of that, around INR3,850 crores debt will move out of these 9 assets. So 8 assets INR3,850 crores.

items.statement: InvIT formation nearing completion with in-principle approval from NSE, BSE, SEBI; launch expected in Q2 FY26 (September)
items.quote: I'm also happy to report that our InvIT formation process is nearing completion and we have received in -principle approval from NSE, BSE and SEBI. After a few more necessary clearances, we are excited and we anticipate to launch the InvIT within this quarter.

items.statement: Coal MDO production: Siarmal 5.4 MMT in Q1 FY26 (target 25 MMT FY26), Pachhwara 2.9 MMT in Q1 FY26 (target 7 MMT FY26), total 32 MMT FY26
items.quote: In our Siarmal MDO, we have achieved a production volume of 5.4 million metric tons in quarter 1 FY '26, and we are on -track to meet our full year target of 25 million metric tons for FY '26. Similarly, our Pachhwara MDO achieved 2.9 million metric tons in quarter 1 of FY '26, positioning us well to reach our full year target of 7 million metric tons for FY '26. In total, we will achieve producti

items.statement: Siarmal CHP capex ~INR900 crore to start in 1-2 quarters when production exceeds 35 MMT
items.quote: CHP out of the total balance capex is around INR900 crores. Without CHP also, we are targeting 25 million tons and next year, 35 million tons. So we will start the CHP capex when we want to go above 35 million tons. So we are well within the targeted total production capacity. So within, you can say, next 1 or 2 quarters, we will start because there is no point doing the capex early than required.

items.statement: Consol EBITDA margin improved due to completed HAM projects and coal business; standalone margin declined due to lower road/water revenue
items.quote: EBITDA margin increased on account of completed HAM projects and coal business performance. Profit after tax increased by 93.7% to INR271 crores from INR140 crores.

items.statement: Current 10-11% EBITDA margin at bottom; expect 300-400 bps improvement when order book fills and fixed costs absorb better
items.quote: Our anticipation, at least when we hope once things are on a regular kind of basis and the order book is fine, full, and we are targeting what we're doing, we're able to fully utilize all our assets. It should be at least a 300 to 400 basis point improvement in an ideal scenario, where I will also look at early completion and all of those things as well.

items.statement: Muted order activity continues across infrastructure sectors; NHAI to bid 124 road projects worth INR3.4 lakh crore in FY26
items.quote: In the road sector, the NHAI is preparing to bid out 124 road projects worth INR3.4 lakh crores in FY '26. These projects will include a mix of HAM, BOT and EPC models.

items.statement: NHAI tightened qualification criteria: assessed net worth (20% of project size deducted from net worth), larger project packages (INR2,000-2,500 crore), already implemented for HAM/EPC
items.quote: Mainly, Ashish ji whatever has changed in the qualification criteria, that is a net worth criteria. Earlier, the size of the project should have a 20% net worth. But now they have driven an assessed net worth. Already, if you have a project of INR5,000 crores, then 20% of that INR5,000 crores will deduct from the existing net worth.

items.statement: Bid ~INR20,000 crore projects across sectors; 60-40 HAM/BOT vs EPC mix expected from NHAI/MoRTH
items.quote: We bid in some different kind of projects, sir. About INR20,000 crores of projects we have bid for right now across different sectors.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 84 from 75 due to 15% revenue decline; absolute inventory stable, expect 75-80 days by year-end
items.quote: So basically, if you see the inventory in absolute terms, the inventory has decreased marginally. But yes, because my sales is down by around 15%. So the 9 days increase in my net working capital days is because my denominator is down, which is the revenue. So in absolute terms, my inventory is not increasing. So it will be more or less same as previous year, and we will end with more or less 75,

items.statement: JJM hydro testing milestone INR450 crore receivable expected in Q3 FY26
items.quote: So once hydro test is done, I can receive the 10% out of these 3 projects, which is primarily INR450 crores, number one. Number two, my -- basically debtor has increased marginally. The sentiment is probably what's coming in the way and seen at times that as festivals start coming in there is a turn in sentiment and we're hoping that the industry in urban starts picking up towards the end of August as the festival seasons get started in some parts of the country and then in September with N

items.statement: Thar ROXX booking pipeline strong, focused on 4x4 variants; waiting period being reduced
items.quote: Thar ROXX has a booking pipeline. So, the booking pipeline is much more of the 4x4 part of the portfolio. You know, as we've said earlier, our intention is to not have long waiting period than booking and that's the endeavor. So, we've ramped up.

items.statement: XUV 3XO export target of 1000+ units per month; launched in Australia with positive response
items.quote: At this point, we're hoping to do roughly 1000+ of 3XO in the export per month.

items.statement: Capacity expansion for new platform within Chakan plant; greenfield site not finalized
items.quote: We have actually been able to pull out more out of the Chakan plant than what we thought. And, hence, while we are exploring the greenfield as an avenue to make us completely future ready, we still have not zeroed in on the site and that we will do over the next few months.

items.statement: ICE capacity utilization ~80% (mid-40s of 55,000 capacity); EV capacity utilization ~70%, ramping to 4,000/month
items.quote: The capacity utilization, I think, you see our numbers right now. We have an ICE capacity of roughly 55,000. We are in the mid-40s, so roughly about 80% or so is our capacity utilization. And it's about the same for Electric Vehicles where we are 70%. In this time, we are ramping up to a level of about 4,000.

items.statement: Steel prices up 6% QoQ; mitigated in Q1 via hedging and inventory; price increases taken
items.quote: So, on the commodity prices, we are concerned about steel going up. Steel has gone up by about 6% over the last quarter. We were able to mitigate some of this in Q1 through hedging and inventory carryovers as well. We have taken some price increases to pass this on to customers as well already.

items.statement: Precious metals inflation emerging due to US pre-buys; monitoring impact
items.quote: And in addition to steel, steel was the largest, there are certain precious metals which are also starting to see some inflation. That could be driven by just overall pre-buys driven by the U.S. So, we will have to watch that as well.

items.statement: EV penetration at ~8% of SUV volumes; E-SUV volume market share 31%; revenue market share 44.3%
items.quote: So, what we're seeing now is our Electric SUV penetration is close to 8%. You can see over the last two quarters, the pace at which penetration is moving up. On the right side, you see the E-SUV volume market share and that has been at a healthy 31%.

items.statement: EV ramp-up to 5-6k/month by festival season; further ramp after Jan 2026 with 2 new products
items.quote: So, just to add, Gunjan, on the ramp up of EVs, we are right now at 4. As we get into festival, we would ramp up to the level of 5 to 6 that we spoke about. And then the further ramp up beyond that we expect to happen after January when we launch the additional 2 products which we have spoken about.

items.statement: EV buyers 80%+ new to Mahindra; highest women ownership in portfolio
items.quote: I don't remember right now the exact number but I think 80 odd percent of our customers who bought Electric Vehicles are not Mahindra.

items.statement: New EV entrants growing market penetration; Mahindra products stack up well; aim to maintain/grow revenue market share
items.quote: We do believe that, you know, that hence our goal should be around the revenue market share because our products will be at much higher average price points than competition.

items.statement: Support SIAM proposal on CAFE norms for PV (Dec 2024) and CV (Jan 2025); high industry alignment
items.quote: given for the Passenger Vehicle business a proposal around the CAFE norms in Mahindra & Mahindra Limited July 30, 2025 December’24 and for the Commercial Vehicle category in January’25. We strongly endorse and support the SIAM proposal and we believe that there is very high alignment within the SIAM organizations around that

items.statement: TREM V panel recommended split implementation by horsepower; comfortable with proposal; awaiting final timelines
items.quote: The government had put a panel in place and they have made a recommendation splitting the kind of implementation needed by different horsepower categories. We believe that is a reasonable proposal and we are comfortable with, you know, an ability to implement that in a manner which is realistic within the rural infrastructure available in the country.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance GNPA at 3.8%, well within thresholds; project initiated to strengthen further
items.quote: Mahindra Finance continues to focus on asset quality at 3.8% is well within the thresholds that the business has set.

items.statement: SUV revenue market share 27.3%, up 570 bps YoY
items.quote: The volume for SUVs is up 22% and revenue market share is at 27.3%, up 570 basis points.

items.statement: Tractor market share 45.2%, up 50 bps YoY; highest ever quarterly share
items.quote: Tractor volumes up 10%. A 50 basis point market share gain to 45.2%.

items.statement: LCV volume market share 54.2%
items.quote: the volume market share in LCV, to a level now 54.2%.

items.statement: Farm Machinery revenue 300+ crores quarterly; Rotavator market share 25%
items.quote: The Farm Machinery business continues to show good growth and we had a 300 crore plus quarter, literally 100 crores per month with Rotavators doing very well, again in market share at 25%.

items.statement: Last Mile Mobility category penetration 28%; volume growth 20%
items.quote: The Last Mile Mobility, we continue our leadership. Category penetration continues to be at a strong level, is now at 28% and the business has seen a growth of 20%.

items.statement: Rare Earth Magnet supply covered for next 2-3 quarters; substitution with Light Earth and ferrites underway
items.quote: We are comfortably covered on the Rare Earth Magnet issue, as we've shared earlier. We have no disruption in production because of that. We've taken a series of actions, some of it has been around inventory, but we are covered comfortably at least for these two quarters, the coming quarter and the next one, and mostly covered on everything for even the fourth quarter of the year.

items.statement: Sampo impairment (Finland harvester) one-time; no further major impact expected
items.quote: the Sampo run rate of impairment is not going to carry into future quarters. These were the two large, we have to Mahindra & Mahindra Limited July 30, 2025 take an impairment in the fourth quarter and we have had to write down assets in the first quarter in anticipation of certain actions that we are taking and this should be the end of anything major coming out of Sampo

items.statement: MLDL acquired Rs 3,500 crores GDV; Susten commissioned 70 MW; Accelo strong revenue and profit growth
items.quote: Lifespaces or MLDL has acquired Rs 3,500 crores of GDV. Susten has commissioned 70 megawatts. And Accelo has seen very strong growth in revenue as well as in profitability.

items.statement: Targets 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, and 100-120 net store additions in FY26
items.quote: So we look at a 50% revenue growth going forward and in that we look at 8% to 10% SSSG so that's from the old stores and 40% revenue growth from the newer stores.

items.statement: Targets 10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin in next 2 years, with 8% as defendable floor
items.quote: So the target is 10%, but anything over 8% is good because even an 8% EBITDA margin gets us a 24%, 25% ROE. But of course the target is to reach 10% in the next 2 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR300 cr for 120 stores plus ~INR40 cr for technology and warehouse
items.quote: So we plan to open 120 stores this year so that is around INR300 crores of capex plus inventory required for those stores. And if you include technology, warehouse; that will be a dditional I think INR40 crores of capex

items.statement: Per store capex ~INR1.1 cr plus ~INR1.3 cr inventory; total ~INR2.4 cr per store
items.quote: No, capex was INR1.1 crores and inventory was about INR1.3 crores paid inventory. So it was always INR2.3 crores to INR2.4 crores and it is still at the same level.

items.statement: Targets 100-120 net store additions in FY26; could rise to 130-150 in FY27 if performance sustains; QIP could add 20-25 stores in FY26 and 30-40 in FY27
items.quote: So this year, initially the target was 100 stores. I think we are on track. We should be opening about 100 to 120. And again the next y ear's target will completely depend on this year's performance. If we have another blowout year like the last 2 years, then next year we will increase the target to 130 to 150 stores

items.statement: 76 stores under active work, 150+ properties shortlisted; 3-6 months from shortlist to opening
items.quote: I think 76 there is still work going on. And if you talk about shortlisted properties, then there are more than 150 properties that are shortlisted.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin 29.4% vs 28.8% YoY; improvement from product mix, lower marketing spend, and 1% saving from fabric cost consolidation
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 29.4% for the first quarter FY '26 as compared to 28.8% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 8.3% from 7.8% YoY; targets 10% in 2 years via operating leverage, higher SSSG, better full-price sales and mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 7.8% to 8.3%.

items.statement: No price increases taken; gross margin improvement from mix, marketing spend reduction, and vendor cost savings; full-price sales 92%
items.quote: So there are 3, 4 things that happened here. So one is definitely product mix. Second, we reduced the overall marketing spend. So a lot of marketing gifts that we give to the customer as a part of bill busters is part of our gross margins. So that had reduced I think 20, 30 basis points. And also we made a cost committee about 6 to 7 months back and because of consolidating fabric purchases and fa

items.statement: Apparel share increased, general merchandise reduced; ASP rose ~15-17% due to mix shift; full-price sales 92%
items.quote: I think that's because of the change in product mix because we have reduced a lot of general merchandize goods whose ASP was really low like INR30, INR40 and apparel contribution has gone up. So that is why we're seeing such a sharp increase in the ASP.

items.statement: Increasing replenishment frequency to every 2 days (some daily) from weekly; targeting store inventory cover of 3-4 days vs 10-12 days currently
items.quote: Currently we keep about 10 to 12 days of sales cover at the store. We plan to bring it down to just 3 to 4 days except the display stock.

items.statement: Plans to repay all ~INR120 cr debt from QIP proceeds; aims to be debt-free
items.quote: Yes, that's what I meant. So if we raise capital, then we will repay all the debt because it doesn't make sense to have that debt if you're raising money through QIP.

items.statement: Enabling resolution passed for QIP up to INR400 cr; proceeds for debt repayment, accelerated store openings, vendor payments, warehouse, technology
items.quote: So we have got an enabling resolution approved and we are planning to raise money. It's not out of necessity or weakness. We're doing it from a position of strength.

items.statement: Logistics cost only 1.1% of revenue; new East warehouse investment INR25-30 cr; new geography entry not margin dilutive
items.quote: No. So our logistic cost is just 1.1% of the total business. So it is not significant enough. Even if we open a new geography, the delta or additional I think logistic cost would never exceed 0.1% or 0.2%.

items.statement: Mobile number as unique customer ID; automated SMS/WhatsApp for retention; data collected at 40-45 attributes per article drives assortment
items.quote: The mobile number is a unique customer ID of each and every customer. So we do a lot of automation in terms of SMS, WhatsApp in order to get that customer back to the stores.

items.statement: Competition intense but Tier 2/3 real estate still abundant; active in 25 states; not facing location constraints
items.quote: So see, competition has become the new reality. We look at it as an external factor that is out of our control. Of course a lot of retailers are opening a lot of stores. But Tier 2, Tier 3 being our main target market, there is still a lot of availability of locations.

items.statement: Hired key managers across functions; business development team grew from 4 to 16; retention bonuses and variable pay up to 50% of salary; attrition reduced
items.quote: So we have hired I think a key manager person in a lot of new departments and our business development team used to be 4 members, now it is 16 members. So similarly, that kind of expansion has happened in each and every team.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS ROE 27.5% in Q1 FY26 vs 23% FY25 and 10.7% FY24; targets 40% ROE at INR1,200 PSF
items.quote: We are proud to report a consistent improvement in ROE, which stood at 27.5% in the first quarter, up from 23% in FY '25 and 10.7% in FY '24.

items.statement: Store expansion phased; next phase contingent on prior phase metrics (new store PSF within 30% of old, SSSG 8-10%); will pause if benchmarks missed
items.quote: So the next phase of expansion is always dependent on the ex ecution of the previous phase. So the day we feel the newer stores are not within the benchmark of 30% of old stores, the old stores SSSG is going down or any of the metrics we see that it's not up to the mark; then we would just postpone and cancel the next expansion phase

items.statement: Omnichannel exploration ongoing but not urgent; expected to contribute max 4-5% of sales when mature
items.quote: We are exploring the omnichannel business. But I had mentioned this earlier that we are still struggling with a good technology partner and it's not of a very urgent priority for us. Even when that omnichannel business gets mature, it would not contribute to more than 4%, 5% of sales looking at the...

items.statement: Expects PAT positive in all quarters of FY26
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be PAT positive in all the quarters.

items.statement: New East zonal warehouse investment INR25-30 cr; hub-and-spoke model with 8 hubs operational
items.quote: Yes. So there will be a total investment of I think INR25 crores to INR30 crores in that new warehouse.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR 750-800 crore with EBITDA margin 12.5-14% and PAT 9-10%
items.quote: So probably, our expected that we are expecting is about probably 750 to 800 crores by the end of this FY 26. And the margins, the EBITDA margin would be around in between probably 12.5 to 14% which will give a PAT of about 9-10% of them.

items.statement: Conservative target of 75% CAGR revenue growth for FY26
items.quote: That's our conservative target, actually, to be precise.

items.statement: FY27 APS revenue expected at INR 1,200-1,300 crore; A Plus Solar Cell revenue INR 600-700 crore in FY28
items.quote: We expect turnover of 1,200 to 1,300 from APS then in 2027-2028, probably we expect standalone turnover of APS and its subsidiary like 100% subsidiary. It would be about in the range of 1,700 to 1,800 crore and there would be INR 600 to 700 crores of turnover from A plus solar cell in 2027-2028.

items.statement: Phase 1 Topcon line (400 MW) CapEx ~INR 85-90 crore including working capital; Phase 2 (400 MW) only machinery ~INR 20-30 crore
items.quote: So probably, the total CapEx for whole 400 megawatt would be, like, say, first half of 400 megawatt, we have already bought the land and building worth about two million dollars. Machinery would be about four million dollars and the working capital, if you notice, then the CapEx would be only six million, but the working capital for this would be required at about 3-4 million.

items.statement: Solar cell plant (1 GW) CapEx INR 900 crore; 30% promoter funded, rest via preferential issue and debt
items.quote: For solar cell. So, solar cell the capacity as you said, 800-900 crore. Out of it, say, for example, I mean the capacity is INR 900 crores, out of which 30%, that is around INR 250-300 crore would be funded by the promoter, APS, and some fund raising too and the rest will come from that.

items.statement: Phase 1 Topcon line (400 MW) commercial production from early October 2025; Phase 2 (400 MW) by Q1 FY27; total 1.2 GW module capacity
items.quote: Our first phase of 400-megawatt Topcon line is set for production by early October 2025. Our second phase for 400-megawatt expansion also will be expected to run by first quarter of FY2627.

items.statement: Current 400 MW Monopark line running at 80-85% utilization; 200 MW poly line isolated
items.quote: Currently, 400 means last three to four months, 400 megawatt Monopark line is up and running, which is we are utilizing almost 80 to 85% of this line.

items.statement: Solar cell plant (1 GW) with 2 GW utility near Ahmedabad expected to start within 18-24 months
items.quote: Initial groundwork for our one-gigawatt solar cell line with two-gigawatt utility near Ahmedabad is also progressing very well, which is expected to, start within 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Solar pump order book INR 275-300 crore; wholesale is cash-and-carry with 75 distributors; retail order book ~9-10 MW at any time
items.quote: we have got the order book for about, say, INR 275 to 300 crores. We already have that order book, you know. And it continues to add on to that every quarter

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 13.91% (up 204 bps YoY); PAT margin 9.59% (up 163 bps YoY); FY26 EBITDA margin guided 12.5-14%
items.quote: EBITDA also grew by 118.60% to 21.32 crore, with an improved margin of 13.91, which was what we were expecting. In our last call also, we said that we are expecting to achieve this margin and we achieved this margin, which is up to 0.204 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Vertical integration via solar cell manufacturing expected to add 100-200 bps to EPS margin
items.quote: It may increase the margin by probably another percent or so. I mean, probably from a 100-basis point to 200 basis point. It will add to the EPS margin.

items.statement: DCR module realization INR 24-25/W (INR 2.4-2.5 cr/MW); non-DCR INR 12-14/W (INR 1.25-1.4 cr/MW)
items.quote: If the non-DCR is currently 1250 to 1350 up to 14, then the DCR is INR 24 to 25 rupees per watt. So, one megawatt is 2.4 to 2.5 crores per DCR. If it is a non-DCR, it's 1.3, 1.2 to 1, means 1.25 to 1.4 crores.

items.statement: No demand issues for next 1-2 years; H1 seasonally slower due to monsoon, H2 stronger
items.quote: So usually like in solar cycle, H1 is always on the slower side, usually and H2 is always better than the first H1 because in during this h one is a monsoon and everything is there

items.statement: Wholesale: 75 distributors (30-35 active 3-4 years); Retail: 12,000+ customers; Pump: 8 states with order book; C&I segment started 3-4 months ago
items.quote: We have got about 75 distributors right now. Out of which, 30-35 are with us. We are buying from us since the last three to four years.

items.statement: Q1 cash flow negative due to INR 10 cr deposit for 150 MW Jupiter cell supply contract and CapEx; expected positive in coming quarters with LC facility
items.quote: bhai just said that we had to pay a handsome amount of deposit for us securing this contract of hundred and fifty megawatt from Jupiter. We paid about 10 crores of deposit. Plus, we had to do our CapEx for our building, plus thirty percent contribution that we had to pay for machinery. So that is why our cash flow is negative

items.statement: Effectively debt-free; INR 5 cr fund-based limit unutilized; INR 20 cr term loan for machinery (subsidized); targeting INR 25 cr fund-based limit by year-end as safety
items.quote: So in effect, I can say that it is a debt free company. Only that we have is a term loan term loan of about right now at the end of the June, it will be about 20 crores because we are buying machinery, that CapEx for the machinery that new coming and the old one.

items.statement: Preferential issue of INR 75-100 cr planned for solar cell plant funding
items.quote: Prefer preferential issue.

items.statement: ALMC program from June 1, 2026 mandates Indian-made solar cells; government pushing for wafer and polysilicon independence within 3 years
items.quote: From 1st of the June 2026, central government is expecting most of the solar cell to be made from India. So, I am hoping 1st phase of the solar cell, we will use 70, at least 60 to 70 percent, and remaining we have to sell to other party.

items.statement: No near-term export plans; focus on domestic demand for 1.2 GW capacity; Australia connections exist but not pursuing
items.quote: I don't think so in near future for 1.2-gigawatt solar panel sales, we need to go to overseas. Even in Australia also, we have very good connections, but I don't think we will be not in a position to export solar panel to overseas.

items.statement: DCR cells sourced from Jupiter (105 MW agreement) and imports; non-DCR cells from China (90% overseas share)
items.quote: the for domestic requirement, we have signed up the agreement with Jupiter for 105 megawatts, and remaining, we are buying from overseas. Achuth Pabbath: I'm from country exactly? Nikunj Patel: China because the China have, like, a 90% overseas market share for production manufacturing

items.statement: China supply risk for wafers/ingots/polysilicon; India targeting self-reliance in 3 years via ALMC and downstream policies
items.quote: See, China currently, still, there's nothing wrong to say if China holds the market, it can affect in near future to India. But take, our government long term future, say, like, if we say from 1st June 2026, they want to bring the ALMC program as well. That means everybody must have to use the Indian made solar cell.

items.statement: Management structure: COO NK Singh, GM Daval Suthar (13 yrs), Sales Director Samir Patel (25-30 yrs), Pump head Pankaj Kumar (20+ yrs), Retail head Jignesh Patel, Factory head Darmendra Patel; Nikunj travels quarterly 15-20 days, Kalpesh in
items.quote: We have our COO, Chief Operating Officer, NK Singh. He looks after our day-to-day requirement. We have a general manager and hold time director, Daval Suthar. He's with company since last 13 years. We have our sales director, Sami r Patel, who have almost 30 years’ experience , 25 years’ experience in sales industry who look after our wholesale division sales

items.statement: A Plus Solar Cell is 51% owned by APS (61% shares held by APS), 49% by promoter Nikunj Patel
items.quote: APS, also the premium solar has got 51% stake right now, and 49% is being held by, the promoter, Nikunj.

items.statement: Diversified across pump, retail, wholesale, C&I, ground-mount reduces realization risk; 1 GW breakeven optimal vs larger undiversified peers
items.quote: with APS, we strategically working in, say, like, pump division, our retail segment, our wholesale segment, our C&I segment, and our ground mounting projects, we put it at the last, not at the first because it's very easy to get one or two big orders from just one of our ten mentioned, Sou mil mentioned, like Coal India or somebody or NTPC, then it can straight away shoot up our revenue, but it ma

items.statement: Targets 20-30% annual revenue growth while maintaining strong margins for FY26
items.quote: going forward, we are targeting an annual growth of 20% to 30% while maintaining strong margins.

items.statement: Planned FY26 capex of INR100 crores for equipment rental segment, INR35 crores already executed in Q1
items.quote: For FY '26, we have outlined a capex of INR100 crores for the equipment rental segment, out of which we have already executed INR35 crores in the quarter.

items.statement: Open to exceeding INR100 crore capex if better opportunities arise, decision by Q3
items.quote: But in case there are better opportunities beyond the INR100 crores capex that is required, we are open to doing that, and the call would be taken when the time is right.

items.statement: Order book of INR157.2 crores as of July 2025, fully executable in FY26, split 61% equipment rental and 39% warehousing
items.quote: As of July 2025, our order book stood at INR157.2 crores, which is executable entirely in FY '26. Of this, 39% is from our warehousing segment and 61% is from the equipment rental segment.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 37.4%, up 370 bps YoY; PAT margin 10.5%, up 100 bps YoY
items.quote: Importantly, we achieved this while growing our EBITDA margin that reached 37.4%, a year -on-year increase of 370 basis points.

items.statement: Equipment rental standalone EBITDA margin 64% in Q1, sustained above 60% expected going forward
items.quote: The overall EBITDA for this segment stood at 57%, while the standalone EBITDA for equipment rentals stood at 64% for the quarter.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts targeting 25% EBITDA margin in FY26, up from 18-20% currently
items.quote: Going forward, the kind of visibility and order book that we have, we are looking at even expanding that to at least 25% and the ideal push would be to go from 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Warehousing & transportation EBITDA margin 17% in Q1, expected to stabilize at 18-20% as transportation share normalizes
items.quote: And with things stabilizing going forward, we should be able to maintain that 18% to 20 -odd percent of margin, which we had earlier maintained before it dropped to 15%, 16%.

items.statement: Robust demand across all operating sectors including cement, steel, power, petrochemical, and renewable energy
items.quote: In the present market scenario, we are witnessing robust demand across all segments and sectors that we operate in.

items.statement: Renewable energy contributed 6% of equipment rental revenue in Q1, targeting 10% for FY26
items.quote: The company is aggressively focusing on expanding its footprint in the renewable energy sector, which is expected to contribute 10% of the equipment rental revenues for FY '26.

items.statement: Fleet size 375 machines as of June 30, 2025; added 7 cranes in Q1; expect 7-12 more machines by year-end
items.quote: As of 30th of June 2025, the company's fleet size stood at 375 machines, aggregating a gross block of INR454.81 crores.

items.statement: Equipment rental capacity utilization at 83% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The capacity utilization for the quarter was at 83%, and the company completed a capex of INR35 crores in Q1 FY '26, adding a total of 7 cranes in the equipment rental segment.

items.statement: Average gross monthly rental yield maintained at 3% in Q1, targeting 2.9-3% range going forward
items.quote: In the equipment rental segment, the average gross monthly rental yield was at 3%, which was at 2.98% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Receivable days reduced to 64 in Q1 from 77 a year ago; target stable range 60-70 days
items.quote: This has led to the receivable days dropping to just 64 from 77 days in the previous year for the same period.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio maintained at 0.92; net cash flow from operations INR16.20 crores in Q1
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio has been maintained at 0.92, while the net cash flow from operations stood at a healthy INR16.20 crores for Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: SAIL Dankuni warehouse contract won, 4.5 years, INR80 crores value; operational by end Q2/start Q3
items.quote: we have won a new contract from the Steel Authority of India Limited, which is for the Dankuni warehouse, which is the highest volume warehouse for Steel Authority in India.

items.statement: SAIL contract expected steady revenue ~INR1-1.5 crores/month; volumes historically meet or exceed contracted levels
items.quote: So if you base on that, the average run rate would be around INR1 crores, INR1.5 crores per month on a monthly basis revenue side.

items.statement: Equipment fungible across sectors; buying fully loaded models to serve multiple industries
items.quote: Similarly, in the case of cranes or other equipment we buy, there is called a fully loaded model, which is the topmost model of that machine. And we usually are buying the fully loaded models of these machines because we want to use them across sectors rather than them being sector -specific.

items.statement: Depreciation expected to stabilize at INR48-50 crores annually for FY26; further changes depend on next year's capex
items.quote: So this should stabilize on a yearly basis at around INR48 crores to INR50-odd crores of depreciation that we see.

items.statement: Capex deployment timeline ~1 month from order to revenue generation
items.quote: And ideally, within 1 month is the timeline, the highest period that we see the revenue coming in from the capex that we have deployed.

items.statement: Warehousing & transportation revenue INR29.5 crores in Q1, up 82% YoY due to low base from labor standoff in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The warehousing and transportation segment registered an 82% year-on-year growth with a revenue of INR29.50 crores.

items.statement: Power & fuel cost increase driven by 82% revenue growth in warehousing segment; repair & maintenance up due to specialized service contracts and older equipment mix
items.quote: So power and fuel primarily is -- has gone up because of the higher revenue in that segment because power and fuel is in our scope as per our contracts.

items.statement: Not an MSME; does not qualify under government criteria
items.quote: No, we are not an MSME, sir, because we do not qualify in the criteria as laid down by the government.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts require specialized manpower deployment alongside equipment
items.quote: We are focusing on services which require the equipment and the specialized manpower along with it that we are able to deploy.

items.statement: Internal credit growth guidance for FY26 is around 13%
items.quote: Yes Sir, our internal guidance is around 13% credit growth for FY26. While Q1 has shown strong momentum (5.5%), It is always better to do beyond whatever is committed.

items.statement: Goal to maintain NIM above 3% despite potential repo rate cuts
items.quote: Our goal is to maintain NIM above 3%, and we are confident we can do so.

items.statement: NIM was 3.04% in Q1 FY26, down from 3.58% in Q4 FY25 due to industry-wide margin pressure
items.quote: Net Interest Margin (NIM) was 3.04% for June 2025, compared to 3.06% in June 2024. Sequentially, NIM decline d from 3.58% in March 2025 due to industry -wide margin

items.statement: Blended RAM yield may go below 9% given recent repo rate reduction and possibility of another cut
items.quote: Given the recent 1% repo rate reduction, and the possibility of another cut, the blended RAM yield may go below 9%. We're closely monitoring this.
