items.statement: Q1 FY26 PAT margin expanded 98 bps YoY and 26 bps QoQ to 6%
items.quote: Profit after tax margin was 6%, experiencing a margin expansion of 98 basis points on yearly basis and 26 basis points on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Export share rose to 58% of revenue in Q1 FY26 from 47% YoY; exports grew ~18% YoY to INR 341 cr
items.quote: Shares of exports in the revenue is approximately INR 341 crores for the quarter. The company had another quarter of strong showing over the export front with an overall mix of sales from the export increased to 58% in Q1 FY '26 from 47% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 95% in Q1 FY26, flat YoY; cotton yarn production 20.9 MT and sales 20.3 MT
items.quote: Capacity utilization at 95% remains at the same level as the Quarter 1 FY '25. Both cotton yarn production and cotton yarn sales remain marginally higher in Quarter 1 FY '26 coming in at 20.9 metric ton and 20.3 metric ton respectively.

items.statement: Indian cotton prices stable but inching up late in quarter due to high CCI inventory, low fresh supply and MSP; international cotton at discount but 11% import duty hurts landed cost
items.quote: On the macro front, despite the Indian cotton being largely stable over the quarter, we observed it to be inching up slowly as the quarter grew to a close. This rise in prices was caused by a combination of factors such as high inventory with the Cotton Corporation of India, lack of fresh supplies in the markets, as well as minimum support prices driving prices higher for buyers.

items.statement: US announced 25% tariff on Indian goods vs 20% on other Asian players; company has limited direct US exposure but indirect exposure via international customers
items.quote: The other key event was the recent declaration of 25% tariff on Indian goods by the USA. The USA is a very important end-user market as far as textile players are concerned. The additional 5% tariff differential as compared to 20% of tariff levied on other Asian players will have some adversary effect on Indian players' pricing edge.

items.statement: Greenfield expansion of 150,000 spindles (~40% increase over 3.8 lakh) in Odisha at ~INR 1,000 cr capex; timeline 12-15 months; funded by internal accruals and term loans
items.quote: We will be undertaking a CAPEX plan of approximately INR 1,000 crores as a part of the Greenfield Capacity Addition Program to increase our spindle count by 150,000 spindles. This is a significant capacity expansion to approximately 40% over the existing spindle count of 3.8 lakhs.

items.statement: Integration of apparel manufacturing and dye house into listed entity within 6-8 months; expects INR 200 cr top-line in first year with better EBITDA
items.quote: So, as we mentioned, that we are confident of achieving the integration of our apparel and dyeing capacity with us in next six to eight months. So, definitely, there will be the top line increase in the first year should be around INR 200 crores. And the EBITDA in that business is slightly better.

items.statement: Bangladesh demand remains good; land route still closed, may open 6-8 months after elections expected in 3-4 months
items.quote: The demand from Bangladesh continues to be good. The land route is still not working. But we expect the elections, Bangladesh is expecting to hold election in the next 3, 4 months. We don't expect the land route to open before that.

items.statement: Over 50% of exports go to Bangladesh; rest to China, Latin America, Europe in single digits; no direct exports to UK or US
items.quote: So, most of our export, more than 50% of our export goes to Bangladesh. Then we export, rest all of the countries are in single digits. So, like China, we do to Latin America and European countries.

items.statement: All Bangladesh exports under LC, paid on time; no CAD business
items.quote: So, we export under LC. All our exports to Bangladesh are under LC, and we get paid on time. So, it is just all under LC business. We don't do any CAD business with them.

items.statement: Long-term debt target INR 700-800 cr max over next 2-3 years; current long-term debt ~INR 300 cr; debt-equity ceiling 0.5-0.7; average interest cost ~7%
items.quote: So, ma'am, our goal is to not go beyond the INR 700 crores, INR 800 crores of long-term debt any time in next two to three years. So, we will stick to that. So, there will be, I think, our long-term debt right now is about INR 300 crores.

items.statement: MoU with Odisha for 300,000 spindles; first phase 150,000; further expansion possible; capex funding mix ~30% equity / 70% debt
items.quote: So, our MoU with Odisha government is for 300,000 spindles. And with the first phase, what we are putting right now is 150,000. Once it's stabilized, we go for the second phase.

items.statement: Expects double-digit EBITDA margins to sustain for next few quarters despite macro headwinds
items.quote: But, yes, we can expect the margins. We expect the margins to stay in double digits for next few quarters given under the present circumstance.

items.statement: Near-term spreads uncertain due to tariff volatility and rising cotton prices; expects clarity in 30-45 days
items.quote: But how the market behaves and how this tariff uncertainty pans out in next two to three months, it is very difficult to answer how the spreads look going forward in next two to three months.

items.statement: Apparel/dyeing integration revenue currently INR 150-180 cr; target to double in 2-3 years post-merger with better margins than spinning
items.quote: And we would like to, right now, our revenue is about INR 150 crores from those units, INR 180 crores. And we expect to double it within the next two to three years.

items.statement: Product mix drives realization difference: synthetic blends sold domestically, cotton yarn exported; international and domestic pricing similar
items.quote: So, the revenue, the pricing in international market or Indian market is almost similar. The only thing is our product mix in our exports and our domestic changes.

items.statement: Government considering removing import duty on cotton; possible duty-free US cotton under bilateral trade talks
items.quote: The government is also contemplating to do away with the import duty. Then we have approached the Ministry many times, and it seems they are serious now. And then, there are different permutations and combinations, how to manage your raw material with less impact of duties and all.

items.statement: Solar power SPV on track to deliver contracted power from 1st March
items.quote: Our SPV for solar power is on target to deliver us the contracted power from 1st March.

items.statement: Chinese competition at 55% tariff may reduce pressure on other countries once tariff uncertainty settles
items.quote: But I know one thing for sure, that after these uncertainties are over, that with China being at 55% and being the major exporter across the world, so I think other countries might not feel as much pain as expected.

items.statement: New consolidated EBITDA margin range estimated at 23.5-25% after Railway acquisition
items.quote: So yeah, 24 to 25 or 23.5 to 25 will be the new EBIDTA rate , but it's just mathematically, just do the arithmetic, we'll get to the numbers.

items.statement: Net order book expanded to ₹262 billion with 75% EV share, highest ever
items.quote: the end of Q1 FY26, our net order book has expanded to ₹262 billion. And the EV portion remains high at 75% of the order book

items.statement: Largest single order in 2.5 years worth over ₹1,500 crores for North American EV platform starting Q3 FY28
items.quote: This is the largest single order win in 2.5 years and adds over 1,500 crores to our orderbook.

items.statement: EV 3-wheeler motor program adds ₹260 crores to order book, starting Q4 FY26
items.quote: This program has added 260 crores to the order book and is expected to start quite soon , actually in Q4 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Q1 worst quarter since IPO due to four temporary factors: EV supply terms change, customer slowdown, rare earth magnet shortage, US tariff uncertainty
items.quote: Q1 was undoubtedly our worst quarter since our IPO. This is mainly due to the convergence of 4 adverse but , in our view, at least temporary factors.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined 4.3% YoY due to adverse operating leverage and product mix, plus Railway acquisition impact
items.quote: The EBITDA margin declined by 4.3%. That's a combination of adverse effects of operating leverage and adverse product mix.

items.statement: China JV with JNT for driveline manufacturing, 60% stake, operations to commence H2 FY26
items.quote: Operations are said to commence in the second half of the current financial year to start fulfilling orders from both EV and Non-EV automotive customers.

items.statement: China JV will start with differential housings and parts, later export gears from India for final assembly in China
items.quote: What we will start off with is supplying differential housings and other parts. We will, at the next phase, which is not yet part of the financial planning right now, but we will in the next phase export gears from here and assemble the final assembly there.

items.statement: BEV revenue share fell to 28% from 33% YoY, BEV revenue declined 25% to ₹2.1 billion
items.quote: BEV revenue share has decreased from 33% in Q1 of last year to 28% and BEV revenue in rupee terms has declined by 25% to 2.1 billion rupees.

items.statement: India became largest end market at 37% revenue share, North America 34%, Asia 8%
items.quote: By geography, now India has already become our largest end market, accounting for 37% of our total revenue. North America follows as our second largest market, contributing 34% and to add , I mean it's a small number, but if you look at how much it has jumped, the share of Asia, primarily driven by China, has increased to 8% from 6% last year.

items.statement: Railway business contributed 8% to revenue in Q1 (3 weeks), non-auto revenue share doubled to 20%
items.quote: The railway business, which is consolidated just for 1 month and actually 3 weeks to be more precise, from the terms of when we actually started registering sales, because the first week was a transition period. It has contributed 8% to our overall revenue.

items.statement: China banned heavy rare earth magnet exports to India from April 8; switched to light rare earth magnets and alternative suppliers, production back to April run-rate by July
items.quote: since 8th April, China has stopped the supply of heavy rare earth magnets to India. This shortage of magnets has affected the production of EV traction motors in India. However, we've started working with alternative motor architectures that do not use heavy rare earth magnets, and we are also expecting a resolution soon on the heavy rare earth front.

items.statement: No heavy rare earth magnet supply since April 8; recovery achieved via light rare earth magnets and design changes, but motors above 10-15 kW remain challenging
items.quote: No, mostly it's light rare earth magnets and so we do not have any HRE magnets supply since 8 April. Zero.

items.statement: Suspension motor growth driven by Chinese EV customer Nio
items.quote: Yeah, suspension motors, that was the fastest growing product, as you well know, there, that is literally the one product in which the customer is also publicly known, so that is the Chinese EV customer, Nio, and that's where the growth came from.

items.statement: US auto tariffs at 25% since early April; estimated 3-4% revenue impact over 12-18 months, no change yet; Mexico facility plans unchanged
items.quote: we see 3 to 4% of revenue impact could be there possibly, but as you know well, you've covered our sector for long enough to know that it happens in 12 to 18 months, even if it does happen, so hasn't yet happened.

items.statement: Working capital turnover declined due to Railway business having higher working capital cycle
items.quote: working capital turnover has come down because the working capital cycle for the Railway Business is higher compared to other existing businesses.

items.statement: Negative net debt reduced due to Railway acquisition purchase consideration payment
items.quote: negative net debt has reduced largely due to discharge of purchase consideration for the Railway Business.

items.statement: 31 EV programs in production (15 matured, 16 ramping), 29 programs not yet in production
items.quote: at the end of Q1, we have 31 EV programs in production, 15 of which have fully matured and have completely ramped up, and 16 are in the ramp-up phase.

items.statement: NOVELIC sensor production to start next year, first product is in-cabin sensing for EV customer, SMT line in Chennai
items.quote: Next year, the sensor production will start actually, so the hardware parts will start rolling out , and there'll be the first product supply starting.

items.statement: Equipmake 350 kW motor commercialization not feasible without heavy rare earth magnets
items.quote: No, that big a motor without magnets, no chance. I mean, I was talking about 10 kilowatt, talking about 350 kilowatt without heavy rare earth, no, next to impossible to solve that problem.

items.statement: Light rare earth magnet supply risk remains as China is source; bigger motors above 10-15 kW still challenging
items.quote: even the light rare earth magnets, the source is China, so I hope they don't now come after this. I hope they go the other way.

items.statement: Jeff Overly succeeded Sanjay Kapoor as non-executive chairman; no change in executive management
items.quote: Sanjay was a non-executive chairman. He has already been succeeded by Jeff Overly, who is our lead independent director, so he is now the non-executive chairman.

items.statement: Railway business expects growth over next 5 years from new products, rolling stock tailwinds, metro and export expansion; no revenue guidance given
items.quote: we do expect the business to grow well over the next few years, but as you know, we don't give any further guidance in terms of revenue, etc. , but w e do expect growth given what we are doing on the products as well as tailwinds in the industry

items.statement: China JV order book not yet added until binding documents signed; term sheet stage only
items.quote: We have not yet started adding the order book, nor will we guide on it. I'll tell you the reason because right now it's a term sheet. Till we sign all the binding documents and all the stuff is done, we don't want to start adding to our order book.

items.statement: Major EV program ramp-ups expected in Q4 FY26, with large launches (200-300 crore/year) over FY26-28
items.quote: I would say Q4 would be the one in which it will happen because a lot of them for this year were more around motors, where there is a month or two of delay already, now there may be a little bit more delay because of that.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 1,000 crores by FY28
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are confident about the opportunities that lie ahead to achieve our revenue goal of INR1,000 crores in FY '28.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 35% plus for FY26
items.quote: I think we have said that it will be 35% plus , if I remember from my investor meet, which happened 2 months back.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 46.0% and PAT margin at 33.9%
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, EBITDA margin was 46.0% and PAT margin was 33.9% underscoring the strength of our business model and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Map-led EBITDA margin improved to 54.8% in Q1 FY26 from 50.1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our Map-led business remained our key growth engine, delivering a strong 26% year-on-year growth with EBITDA margin of 54.8% as against 50.1% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Automotive and mobility tech revenue grew 24.4% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: From an industry lens, our automotive and mobility tech (A&M) revenue grew 24.4% year-on-year, supported by growing demand for our advanced automotive solutions.

items.statement: Consumer Tech & Enterprise Digital Transformation segment grew 16.1% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The Consumer Tech & Enterprise Digital Transformation (C&E) segm ent also performed well, registering a 16.1% year-on-year increase

items.statement: Strategic business agreement with Zepto for SDK and API integration signed in August 2025
items.quote: In August 2025, we entered into a strategic business agreement with Zepto, a leading quick commerce company, where MapmyIndia SDK and API will be utilized to enhance the customer and delivery experience.

items.statement: Board approved INR 25 crores strategic investment in Zepto on August 7, 2025
items.quote: Additionally on August 7, 2025, the Board has approved a strategic financial investment of INR25 crores in Zepto.

items.statement: Increased shareholding in Gtropy Systems from 75.98% to 96.0% with option to acquire remaining 4% in 4 years
items.quote: The company believes in the long-term prospects of its IoT business and is increasing its shareholding in its IoT subsidiary, Gtropy Systems Private Limited from 75.98% to 96.0%.

items.statement: Cash balance of INR 676 crores as of June 30, with INR 70 crores outflow for Zepto, Gtropy investments and dividend
items.quote: I'll give you the full figure. INR 676 crores as of 30th June. Now three major cash outflows either have happened or is going to happen shortly. One is Zepto, which is INR25 crores. One is Gtropy, another INR25 crores and the INR20 crores dividend which is getting paid right now.

items.statement: INR 233 crores e-commerce order win has started contributing to revenue
items.quote: Let me answer the second part, yes, it has.

items.statement: TerraLink Technologies JV build phase going well, revenues expected from start of FY27
items.quote: And that build phase is going well. Of course, the anchor customers, there would be the parent company of Hyundai AutoEver, but conversations are also on with other OEMs. And that this is in the next 1, 2, 3 years. So start of FY '27 onwards, the TLT revenues will also start coming in, in a good way.

items.statement: Mappls DT subsidiary fully operationalized for government and defense digital transformation and digital twin
items.quote: Mappls DT Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, has been fully operati onalized to serve the large and fast-growing digital transformation and digital twin needs of the government and defense sectors.

items.statement: Government and defense wins across central, state, local levels including defense tech solutions
items.quote: In terms of wins, again, you would have seen the C&E part of the highlights, especially on the government side - lots of new wins across central state and local governments, including also in defense, covering our Map-led, IoT-led, digital twin, digital transformation and defense tech set of solutions.

items.statement: IoT business undergoing transition with management change, inventory rationalization, and contribution margin focus
items.quote: We transitioned the management in the beginning of Q1. And so we're going through this transition period where we are refocusing the business on the way MapmyIndia has been doing in the enterprise world, which is higher margin, large enterprises and having certain fiscal prudencies in mind.

items.statement: International revenues from MapmyIndia have started flowing, expected to become sizable in 1-2 years
items.quote: For MMI from international, revenues have already started to come in, and it will only increase over the time that to come. We are having wins every quarter. Of course, for it to become sizable enough, it will probably take, like we said, about a year or 2, but it will become sizable then.

items.statement: JV TerraLink Technologies expected to start generating revenues by end of FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: For the JV also we've talked about that - end of FY '26 or Q1 FY '27 is when the JV will start also generating revenues.

items.statement: Gtropy management transitioned at beginning of Q1 FY26, focusing on higher margin enterprise business
items.quote: Until March, the management of Gtropy was being run by the earlier founder. We transitioned the management in the beginning of Q1. And so we're going through this transition period where we are refocusing the business on the way MapmyIndia has been doing in the enterprise world, which is higher margin, large enterprises and having certain fiscal prudencies in mind.

items.statement: Conscious effort to run down Gtropy inventory without affecting contribution margin
items.quote: We also felt that the inventory that we had on hand in Gtropy was a bit too high compared to what our comfort factor would be. So we wanted to run down the inventory a little bit, but without affecting the contribution margin.

items.statement: Focus on increasing contribution margin in IoT hardware sales, shied away from some hardware sales
items.quote: We want to see the contribution margin in our IoT business, especially around hardware sales go up. And so there's a conscious effort to increase contribution margin.

items.statement: Competitive advantage in digital twin as product-platform-API solutions company vs services-only players
items.quote: Remember, we are products & platforms and API solution company, and we've been doing this digital twin data maybe without tagging it as such. And if you see the wins that we are doing, most of the wins that we have with the government have an element of digital twin already, whether it is local or state level.

items.statement: Business should be observed on yearly basis due to seasonality, Q4 typically highest quarter
items.quote: At the same time, we would like to communicate that the nature of this business is such that it should be observed more on a yearly basis rather than quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Commissioned 158-bed Raipur hospital on May 2, 2025, taking network to 719 beds across five hospitals
items.quote: On the 2nd of May 2025, we commissioned a 158-bed facility at Pachpedi Naka in Raipur. This facility has been established in an asset-light model and it's fully operational.

items.statement: Signed MoU for 150-bed Jamshedpur hospital with INR60 crore investment, targeting commissioning by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: Additionally, as we had earlier stated, we have signed an M oU for a hospital in Jamshedpur, which will have a planned capacity on 150 beds and an investment outlay of approximately INR60 crores. This hospital is expected to be commissioned by the end of calendar year '26

items.statement: Targeting 1,000 beds in next 2-2.5 years; currently at 719 beds with Jamshedpur adding 150 beds
items.quote: we remain firmly committed to our goal of becoming 1,000 beds in the next 2 years. Thi s target reflects our broader vision of scaling up operations and bringing quality healthcare to more

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue guidance of INR460+ crores implying ~15% growth; ex-Raipur core hospitals expected to grow ~10%
items.quote: So for us also, we are on track to do a 15% plus kind of growth for the full year. The -- sorry, the Howrah hospital just started. So that's why it was not a full quarter for them. So just 1.5 years -- 1.5 months, sorry. So I think that we are still on tra ck to achieve a 460 -plus kind of revenue for the full year, which will be a 15% kind of growth number.

items.statement: Ex-Raipur revenue growth guided at ~10% for FY26
items.quote: Ex Raipur will be about 10%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA INR18.9 crore at 17.9% margin; excluding Raipur losses of INR4.5 crore, steady-state EBITDA ~22%+
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR18.9 crores with an EBITDA margin of 17.9%. This was an account of initial losses for the new Raipur hospital of approximately INR4.5 crores. Excluding these losses, the EBITDA would stand at our steady-state EBITDA of almost 22% plus.

items.statement: Mature hospitals (4 older assets) expected to deliver 22.5-23% EBITDA margin for FY26; Raipur to incur losses
items.quote: The margins would be around 22.5% to 23% for the 4 older assets. And obviously, there will be a loss in Raipur.

items.statement: Raipur hospital expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven in 12-15 months; full-year FY26 loss estimated at INR8 crore
items.quote: So in this quarter, we have done about INR4.5 crores. For the full year, we anticipate the loss to be at around INR8 crores.

items.statement: Raipur hospital at 7% occupancy in Q1 (1.5 months), now running ~15% month-on-month; strong demand sensed in new geography
items.quote: Despite only 1.5 months, Raipur showed for an occupancy of 7% with an ARPOB of INR39,180, and we are on track to achieve EBITDA breakeven in 12 -15 months even though it's a new geography for us. This hospital has immense potential, and there is enough demand that we are sensing in the market.

items.statement: Agartala occupancy improved to 52% from 46% YoY; expected to reach 60% by March FY26 with radiation oncology ramp-up
items.quote: The occupancy of the hospital is back to 50% plus at 52% from 46% on its path to become a mature hospital. It's new speciality seeking in. The ARPOB was also increased to INR35,600 from INR33,700 last year.

items.statement: Salt Lake occupancy improved to ~60% with ARPOB rising to INR42,313 from INR39,200 YoY; 200 bps occupancy increase
items.quote: ILS hospital Salt Lake, our 85 -bed center of surgical accidents continues to perform well and has delivered a strong performance with ARPOB further increasing to INR42,313 from INR39,200 last year, coupled with increase in occupancy by 200 basis points.

items.statement: Dum Dum occupancy at 60%, down from 70% YoY due to conscious reduction in kidney transplants; ALOS reduced to 4.59 from 4.62
items.quote: Dum Dum, the revenue has dipped slightly, but that's again on account of the change in the case mix. We expect Dum Dum occupancy to also ramp up by the end of the year. Dum Dum, the ALOS has reduced further to 4.59 compared to 4.62 in March.

items.statement: Howrah occupancy at 39%, up from COVID lows; robotic knee surgeries started (12 in Q1); targeting 50% by March FY26
items.quote: The Howrah hospital continues to grow from a revenue and patient volume perspective with ARPOB of INR35,600. We have also commenced robotic knee surgeries at this hospital. In Q1 FY '26, the hospital performed 12 surgeries using the robot.

items.statement: Insurance contracts revised every 3 years; no price increase due this FY, next revision expected next year
items.quote: In terms of medical, the contracts with these insurance companies, they contracts get revised every 3 years. So the increase in the prices do not happen every year or every quarter. They happen once in 3 years, and that is not due in this financial year. So that will only kick in next year in terms of medical increase in prices for the insurance patients, which is a bulk of our business.

items.statement: Conscious shift at Dum Dum away from kidney transplants (32 in Q1 vs ~50 previous quarter) toward shorter-stay specialties; renal transplant mix reduced
items.quote: Renal transplants, we've done 32 surgeries in Q1 FY '26. This was -- in the previous quarter, it was about close to 50.

items.statement: Agartala oncology unit (medical + radiation) started March/May 2025; expected INR10-15 crore revenue with 20%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: Oncology unit Agartala would do revenue of almost INR10 crores to INR15 crores for the full year. And profitability for the unit would also be along the similar lines for Agartala, which is about 20-plus kind of EBITDA.

items.statement: Jamshedpur hospital INR60-65 crore capex on rental (build-to-suit) model; 7th hospital capex INR65 crore if asset-light or INR100+ crore if organic
items.quote: So the seventh hospital, we are still on the verge of finalizing, still not finalized. If it's an asset life, then the capex would be around INR65 crores. If it's an organic opportunity, then it could be INR100-odd crores.

items.statement: ALOS improved to 3.4 days from 3.54 days network-wide; ongoing case mix optimization and throughput enhancement
items.quote: improved to 3.4 days from 3.54 days, a result of our ongoing effort to optimize the case mix and enhance throughput.

items.statement: Expected credit loss provisions at ~1.5% of revenue (INR5.8 crore in FY25); management expects stabilization around 1% benchmarked to peers
items.quote: Most of our peers that we have at least seen is at 1%, it's not at 0.25%. I would -- I can stand to be corrected, but most of them that we have seen at almost 1%. We had benchmarked this

items.statement: Network ARPOB INR38,913; Raipur INR39,180, Salt Lake INR42,313, Agartala INR35,600, Dum Dum INR42,684, Howrah INR35,600
items.quote: Our ARPOB stood at INR38,913 aligning with our focus to serve the middle to high- income segment. Approximately 94% of our business continues to come from cash insurance patients, reflecting the strong -- strength of our neighborhood tertiary care model

items.statement: Network bed occupancy 42% (diluted by new Raipur); mature hospitals targeting 60-65% by March FY26
items.quote: Bed occupancy, overall, at the network level stands at 42% due to the addition of a new hospital in Raipur. Now coming to the hospital-wise performance.

items.statement: FY26 occupancy targets: Agartala 60%, Howrah 50%, Salt Lake 65%, Dum Dum 65%, Raipur 20% by March; Jamshedpur ARPOB expected INR35,000-38,000
items.quote: Agartala by at the end of the year, we see it hitting the 60% mark. Howrah hopefully, the 50% mark; Salt Lake around 65% and 65% for Dum Dum as well. Raipur, right now, we're getting at 15%. And by March, we should be closer to 20% for Raipur as well. So this would be the -- in terms of the occupancy forecast for the year, and we expect the assets to perform accordingly. In terms of ARPOB for Jams

items.statement: Competition acknowledged from Narayana/Apollo in Kolkata; low doctor attrition and popular consultants providing defense; service upgrades ongoing
items.quote: In terms of competitive intensity, obviously, competition is there. There are peers which are setting up new assets. And -- but having said that, our doctors and consultants are quite popular, and we are seeing a lot of traction for them as well. The attrition for our doctors is also quite low. So we don't face -- we don't anticipate much of a challenge there.

items.statement: Doctor cost at 26-28% of sales (higher vs peers due to classification differences and Raipur full-time hires); expected to stabilize at 24-25% with occupancy scale-up
items.quote: So it depends on how many of the industry peers classify doctor fees. Some people put it as part of the employee benefit expenses, some people put it as part of doctor payout. We generally put it as part of doctor payout. There are some industry peers who also put it as part of the employee benefit expenses. So this number has been around 25%, 26% for us constantly, slightly higher this quarter be

items.statement: Tax regime evaluation ongoing: old regime offers 100+ bed hospital deduction in cities; new regime at 25% but loses this benefit; consultants mandated to advise
items.quote: So we are evaluating that because there are some tax benefits available for a new hospital when it is set up in terms of any hospital in the city with more than 100 beds, that is not available in the new regime. In the old regime, it is available that are tax consultants, we have given them the mandate to advise and see whether we should be able to -- which would be the more beneficial option.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest impacted Agartala cross-border patient flow; resolution expected to restore occupancy; radiation oncology added to capture local oral cancer demand
items.quote: Agartala has also faced a lot of issues with respect to this Bangladesh unrest. So that is why some of the patients that are coming from Bangladesh had also stopped for the last almost a year. So that is why the dip slightly dip in the occupancy in Agartala. Agartala, we are quite hopeful that this Bangladesh will get resolved and the occupancy, we will start seeing patients again from there.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20-25% for FY26 and coming years
items.quote: Yes, really. We are exploring to 20% to 25% growth on the – already we reached the same this quarter and coming years also, we are going to maintain the same growth.

items.statement: Export revenue mix target of 12-15% for FY26
items.quote: I think we are expecting 12% to 15%.

items.statement: Long-term export revenue mix target of 40% over 10 years
items.quote: Over a period of 10 years down the line, our objective is to maintain 40% from exports and 60% from domestic.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be maintained at current levels for FY26
items.quote: We will continue to maintain the same EBITDA margin. And we will put our honest and best efforts to continue the same EBITDA margins in the future as well.

items.statement: INR 40-50 crore capex for automation and robots in existing facilities over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Existing facilities, we are coming 1 year, 1.5 year, we are going to invest another INR40 crores to INR50 crores on the automation and robots, building and everything.

items.statement: INR 150-180 crore greenfield capex for heavy engineering facility over 15-18 months
items.quote: And a new greenfield project we started already. This is progressing, started progressing, but that we are going to invest another INR150 crores to INR180 crores.

items.statement: Glass lining facility at 50% utilization, metal divisions at 65-70% utilization
items.quote: Current we are using glass lining facility @ 50% and our metal divisions also almost on 60%-70%.

items.statement: Existing facilities capacity to increase three-fold after INR 40-50 crore automation capex
items.quote: Based on that, these existing facilities we can produce threefold, we are increasing threefold manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: New greenfield facility equivalent to all existing facilities combined, doubling revenue potential
items.quote: That facility we are going to, we are expecting, whatever existing facility, all existing facilities equivalent to that new facility. So almost double the revenue.

items.statement: Shell and tube glass-lined heat exchanger production of 300 units per month from January 2026
items.quote: From the month of January onwards, we are going to produce 300 heat exchangers per month.

items.statement: Order book almost full for this year, 90% of order book filled
items.quote: And also, this year, almost 90% of our order book is full.

items.statement: Received 250 orders for shell and tube glass-lined heat exchangers this year
items.quote: We launched this product in first quarter this year, but we got some 250 orders this year.

items.statement: Export EBITDA margin contribution around 25%, better than domestic
items.quote: Export is 25% of EBITDA. Okay. Slightly compared to domestic, export margin is always better.

items.statement: PTFE-lined equipment margins at 8.5% due to product and customer mix
items.quote: Mix of the products and customers.

items.statement: Overall margins to increase slightly once shell and tube heat exchangers are fully launched
items.quote: Once the heat exchangers are launched full-fledged, our margins are going to increase. That is my stand.

items.statement: Domestic launch of shell and tube glass-lined heat exchangers with strong initial orders from key clients
items.quote: One of the most exciting developments this quarter is the domestic launch of our Shell and Tube Glass Lined Heat Exchangers.

items.statement: Exclusive license from AG Japan for shell and tube glass-lined heat exchangers, only company in India with this technology
items.quote: We are manufacturing shell and tube glass lined heat exchangers through AG Japan license. This part no one has in India, even the world also.

items.statement: Working with almost 90% of top CDMO companies in India, 25 top clients
items.quote: All top CDMO companies, almost 90% companies are working with Standard Glass.

items.statement: BioCon Solutions partnership for exclusive distribution in Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore
items.quote: BioCon is our exclusive agent for markets such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Singapore.

items.statement: US subsidiary Standard Engineering Inc. incorporated in South Carolina to support IPP distributor
items.quote: We have incorporated Standard Engineering Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary in South Carolina, USA. This subsidiary has a clear purpose that is to support IPP.

items.statement: Tariff impact of 18-20% analyzed but still cheaper than US manufacturing, no margin pressure expected
items.quote: We analyzed compared to our cost, that is I think we are going to face 18% to 20% impact, but still we are cheaper compared to U.S. manufacturing cost.

items.statement: Working capital at 173 days, targeting reduction to 150 days
items.quote: Working capital remains well managed at 173 days, reflecting our disciplined control on receivables and inventory.

items.statement: Automation and faster delivery expected to help reduce working capital days to 150
items.quote: We are trying to bring down to 150 days. More than that we can't

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents of INR 209 crores providing financial flexibility
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalent stand at INR209 crores, providing significant financial flexibility.

items.statement: No current M&A plans but will consider right opportunities, CPK and Standard Flora subsidiaries showing sales growth
items.quote: Right now, present, we don't have any plans. But if the right opportunity comes, we will definitely consider and we will proceed.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty discussed with distributor IPP, existing orders unaffected, future orders may be discussed
items.quote: But we are discussing with our distributor, IPP. They are not raising any questions till date, but we'll see. But I am confident this is not going to impact anything.

items.statement: FY26 thermal power plant annual average PLF guided at 80%
items.quote: Power also because last year, it was only for the part of the year -- for the whole year, you can assume 80% PLF.

items.statement: FY26 steel volumes expected to remain stable similar to FY25
items.quote: So far as volumes are concerned, steel volumes will remain more or less same -- slightly here and there. Whatever improvement is there on account of the efficiencies, that will be there. Otherwise, steel volumes are stable.

items.statement: FY26 power segment EBITDA per unit guided at INR2 +/- 0.50
items.quote: EBITDA will depend upon the electricity pricing, which is varies in the range and EBITDA may range somewhere about INR2. Plus minus 50 paisa.

items.statement: Annual capex planned at INR500-1,000 crores for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are spending about INR500 crores to INR1,000 crores a year on the expansion projects in different segments, whether it is coal mines, hydropower project and other projects.

items.statement: 50 MW captive solar plant commissioning expected in FY26
items.quote: Captive solar power, 50 megawatts. Most of the equipment has been delivered and transmission line work is ongoing. Project commissioning is expected in current financial year.

items.statement: 30 MW TG set replacement operations expected by mid-FY27 with shutdown in next quarter
items.quote: 30-megawatt TG set replacement. Work is on schedule with operations expected to begin by mid-FY '27. We'll be taking shutdown of the unit in next quarter.

items.statement: Kotaiveera 25 MW hydropower project work expected to begin next quarter
items.quote: Kotaiveera Hydropower project, 25 megawatt. The project is in approval stage with work expected to begin in next quarter.

items.statement: Mineral wool plant commissioning expected in FY26
items.quote: FY '26 will benefit from full year operations of the IPP power plant, increased coal production and the commissioning of three new projects, which are 25-megawatt Rehar hydropower plant, which commissioned in July 2025 , mineral wool plant and 50 -megawatt captive solar power plant.

items.statement: Gare Palma IV/7 coal washery capacity increased from 0.96 to 1.8 million tons with consent to operate received in May 2025
items.quote: Gare Palma IV/7, we have received consent to operate for increased capacity of coal washery from 0.96 million tons to 1.8 million tons in May 2025.

items.statement: Final approval for increasing coal mining capacity from 1.68 to 1.8 million tons expected this quarter
items.quote: Final approval for increasing coal mining capacity from 1.68 million tons is expected this quarter.

items.statement: Shahpur West mine production expected before end of next financial year
items.quote: Shahpur West mine development work is progressing as per schedule and production is expected before the end of the next financial year.

items.statement: Rehar 25 MW hydropower project commercial operation began 8 July 2025
items.quote: Rehar Hydropower project, 25 megawatt. The commercial operation began on 8th July 2025.

items.statement: IPP thermal plant achieved 90.21% PLF in Q1 FY26 vs 71.65% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our IPP thermal power plant achieved significantly improved plant load factor of 90.21% in Q1 as against 71.65% in Q1 FY '25, largely due to ongoing operational efficiency measures.

items.statement: Hydropower generation grew 37% YoY in Q1 FY26 supported by early monsoon
items.quote: Hydropower generation grew by 37% Y -o-Y, supported by early monsoon.

items.statement: Terminated 113 MW hydropower PPA with CSPDCL to sell in open market
items.quote: We strategically terminated the long-term power purchase agreement executed with CSPDCL for 113-megawatt hydropower project. This now gives us the opportunity to sell power in open market, which we believe will be beneficial over the long term.

items.statement: Open market realization for terminated hydro PPA expected at INR5+/- annually
items.quote: Average, it depends season-to-season, it will vary, but it should be somewhere in the range of INR5 plus/minus.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 thermal power realization at INR6.16/unit, but annual average expected lower due to seasonality
items.quote: This what we earned in the first quarter may not be the right number for the whole year. Definitely, generally, first quarter is always better because of the summer seasons.

items.statement: Hydropower average selling price in Q1 around INR5+ per unit
items.quote: We don't have immediately, but it should be somewhere in the range of INR5.

items.statement: Steel demand expected to improve post-monsoon as construction activity picks up
items.quote: So we are hoping that now with consumption pattern g oing forward with the monsoons getting over, the prices also will improve along and the demand also will improve

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA INR627 crores vs INR382 crores YoY, energy segment contributing larger share
items.quote: Operating EBITDA rose to INR627 crores versus INR382 crores Y-o-Y with the Energy segment contributing larger share.

items.statement: Steel division Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 18%, no one-off items, expected to sustain and improve
items.quote: No, there was no one-off item in the steel division. Yes, volume had also gone up as compared to the March. In the March, there were certain shutdowns in the plant. So Steel division, there is no one-off item, and we should be able to sustain and improve from here.

items.statement: Net consolidated debt fell to ~INR1,000 crores from ~INR1,600 crores; long-term loans repayable within year INR206 crores
items.quote: Net consolidated debt, including working capital loans, fell to ~ INR1,000 crores from ~ INR1,600 crores. Long -term loans repayable within the next year stands at INR206 crores.

items.statement: INR1,000 crore debt raise resolution is only enabling, no immediate fundraise plans
items.quote: This is only an enabling resolution. Companies with AA and above ratings are required to part finance their working capital requirement through market listed borrowings. So it is only enabling resolution. We don't have any plan as such to raise any funds.

items.statement: No QIP or fundraise plans in immediate future
items.quote: We don't have any plan of fundraise. In immediate future there is no such plan.

items.statement: Indonesia coal mine expansion planning targeting 1 million tons in near future
items.quote: So we have an operating a mine in Indonesia for that expansion planning is going on and God willing we will try to achieve 1 million ton in near future in that mine -- coal mine and wherever opportunities will come we are open for any opportunity.

items.statement: Indian crude steel production grew 10.3% YoY to 40.6 million metric tons in Q1 CY25
items.quote: India recorded 10.3% growth in crude steel production to 40.6 million metric tons with 8% growth in finished steel demand.

items.statement: Chinese steel exports surged with net exports exceeding 53 million tons Jan-May 2025 pressuring global pricing
items.quote: Despite this, Chinese exports surged with net exports exceeding 53 million tons during January to May '25, putting pressure on global pricing.

items.statement: Targeting INR60-80 crore material cost savings in FY26 from Alvarez & Marsal project, with full INR200 crore recurring savings over time
items.quote: Out of the INR200 crores plan, INR85 crores will be -- approximately about INR85 crores will get in the fiscal year '26 and we are on track of that.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margin in FY26 despite Q1 miss
items.quote: Our intent is to hit double-digit EBITDA in this financial year.

items.statement: Planning chain manufacturing plant for aftermarket vertical, targeting completion in 8-10 months
items.quote: We are setting the organization right, which we will complete by the next 30 to 45 days. And thereafter, we are going for -- and we hope to put up this plant in the next 8 to 10 months.

items.statement: Planning new greenfield stamping facility in North India for OEM proximity
items.quote: We are also planning a new facility in north of India, because most of the big OEMs are there, including Maruti, Hero Motors, HMSI. So we are planning a new greenfield facility here.

items.statement: Front loader capacity 85,000/month, targeting 95-100% utilization in Aug-Oct; top loader 60,000/month at ~90% utilization; AC 65,000/month; refrigerator plant 1M capacity at 50% peak, targeting 60-65%
items.quote: As far as the front loader is concerned, we can make about 85,000 washing machines in a month, and we'll be touching about 95% to 100% capacity in the season ahead both in August and September and October.

items.statement: Q1 gross margin dipped slightly YoY due to commodity price increases (copper, GP, Gas) and 3% INR depreciation, partially offset by cost innovation
items.quote: Compared to quarter 1 of last year, there is an increase in commodity prices, which is mainly in copper, GP, Gas and also, there is an INR depreciation against U.S. dollar, which is around 3%.

items.statement: Expecting INR15-20 crore cost innovation savings in Q2, continuing through year
items.quote: The quarter 2 innovation, what we are expecting is, it will be to the tune of maybe about INR15 crores to INR20 crores, and in line with the target whatever we have taken for the fiscal year.

items.statement: Fixed cost and warehousing/logistics savings expected from Q3 FY26 via Alvarez & Marsal project
items.quote: We expect that the savings will start coming in from Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: AC volumes dropped to 120,000 units in Q1 FY26 from 137,000 YoY due to early monsoon; industry down 30%+
items.quote: During the quarter, we have sold 1,15,000 air conditioners against last year 1,29,000. And as far as OEM is concerned, we have sold 9,800 air conditioner versus last year 6,600.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% front loader growth, 35% top loader growth, 25-30% AC growth for FY26
items.quote: In the top loader, we have been able to -- with the launch of new range, we have been able to grow at a much higher level and have been able to gain the share. Here we envisage around 35-odd percent growth for us.

items.statement: Engineering division targeting INR400-445 crore new orders in fine blanking by March 2027, including brake disc line and sprocket business expansion
items.quote: We are aiming to grow it INR400 crores by the end of -- by March '27 new orders into the pipeline. INR445 crores by March '27.

items.statement: Engineering division planning 30%+ organic growth annually plus M&A; evaluated 48 companies for acquisition
items.quote: The plan is that we have to grow organically, minimum 30% per annum. And also we have to grow through merger and acquisition route, which we are actively pursuing. And we have already seen 48 companies.

items.statement: Commodity price control slipped in Q1; pricing committee now corrected to mitigate future increases
items.quote: What we could have done better is the control on the commodity pricing. We have pricing committee with regular follow-ups and why the commodity pricing and what measures we can take to mitigate that we do it properly, we have now corrected.

items.statement: Compressor supply secured for current season requirements despite industry demand-supply gap
items.quote: We are aware of the demand-supply gap in compressor, but we are already discussing with a manufacturer. And as of today, we are secured with the quantities whatever is required in the -- for the season.

items.statement: Refrigerator mix shifting toward higher-end no-frost models; launching 328-liter model soon
items.quote: We are launching the 328-liter very soon. And after that, we will launch other models. Our brand prism ideally should have -- I mean, our ideal structure would have been to launch the higher-end models first.

items.statement: Washing machines fully transitioned to BLDC motor-driven technology
items.quote: We have moved completely to BLDC. We are moving completely to BLDC.

items.statement: Strengthening consumer finance and affordability team to improve credit card tie-ups and reduce cost
items.quote: We are working on this. As you said, we are strengthening our team on consumer finance and affordability so that our cost has to further go down.

items.statement: AC market has 40+ brands; IFB at 3-3.5% market share but in top 10 price points; front load washer #1 in customer selling price
items.quote: In air conditioners, as you know, it is a crowded market. There are more than 40 brands operating. If you look from the price point, we are in top 10.

items.statement: Government import restrictions on chains prompting domestic chain manufacturing plant investment
items.quote: Now the government is imposing some restriction on imports, so our Board has cleared our investment for setting up a chain manufacturing plant in India.

items.statement: E-waste provisioning at INR2 crore/month (INR24-25 crore annually) included in cost base
items.quote: Our monthly cost is around INR2 crores. So annually is around INR24 crores to INR25 crores.

items.statement: IFB Refrigeration (41% stake) consolidation planned in next 6-12 months subject to Board approval
items.quote: Hopefully, we will get there soon. And we hope to at least consolidate it in the near term. Near term meaning maybe in the next 6 to 12 months, hopefully, subject to Board approvals.

items.statement: Engineering division FY25 margins benefited from stable commodity prices; steel prices up INR3,000 in Q1 FY26 with quarter to half-year pass-through lag
items.quote: The last 2 years, we have been blessed with a stable commodity price, it has not been very -- now in quarter 1 this year, the steel prices have been increased by INR3,000.

items.statement: Change management and cost control execution described as 'very, very slow'; commodity team defocused during A&M project causing slippages
items.quote: Whilst we were working with A&M on cost down, the team that was supposed to handle commodity price, etcetera, got defocused and some slippages have happened there.

items.statement: Fixed cost consolidation slower than required; increments given but work consolidation delayed
items.quote: Areas where consolidation of work, etcetera, should have happened, have not happened as fast as it should have. And that's also an area of slippage.

items.statement: Advertising spend clarified at INR100 crore annually (not INR284 crore); includes CSR and customer sales representative costs from IFB Appliances and Genius
items.quote: Our ad and promo cost annually is around INR100 crores and we are working on reducing the ad and promo -- optimizing the ad and promo cost by increasing the visibility with the same spend.

items.statement: Total customer sales representatives increased to ~4,600 (4,000 IFB Appliances + 600 Genius)
items.quote: The total number will be around 4,600-odd 600 are on Genius folks.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guided at 18-20% for FY26
items.quote: Entire -- we are optimistic for the entire year, but we will stick to our guidance, okay, where we say that, okay, growth will be somewhere between 18% to 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 17-18% for FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 17.8%, at the upper end of our guided range of 17%-18%.

items.statement: Gross margin guided at 42-45% for FY26
items.quote: We feel that the gross margin should steadily be somewhere between 42% to 45%, okay.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected at 130-135 days on annualized basis
items.quote: I think it should streamline over the annualized basis which we feel that it should stay effective between 130 to 135 days.

items.statement: Other income annualized guidance of INR30-35 crore
items.quote: Overall basis, annualized figure, I think, the other income should stay somewhere between INR30 crores, INR35 crores.

items.statement: SSG annualized target of 7-8% for FY26
items.quote: Even when we plan out, we generally plan that annualized basis should be between 7%-8%.

items.statement: Store capex estimated at INR4,000-4,500 per sq ft (INR2,000 capex + INR2,000 opex)
items.quote: Whenever a franchisee comes, we envisage that the investment should be around INR4,000 to 4,500 per square feet. Where INR2,000 is capex and INR2,000 rupees is opex.

items.statement: Spring-Summer 2026 trade show feedback encouraging, strong visibility for H2 booking
items.quote: We also saw encouraging feedback from our recent Spring-Summer 2026 trade show across all our major brands like Killer, Easies, Kraus, Junior Killer and Integriti, which give us strong visibility for H2 booking and channel confidence.

items.statement: Consolidated volume grew 46.4% YoY; standalone volume grew >10% YoY
items.quote: Notably, volume growth of Ap parel on a consolidated basis came in at 46.4% year -on-year, reflecting strong consumer demand and improved market penetration

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA INR42 crore, up 50.6% YoY; margin 17.8% at upper end of guidance
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR42 crores, a growth of 50.6% year-on-year. EBITDA margin stood at 17.8%, at the upper end of our guided range of 17%-18%.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped to 42% due to channel and category mix changes including Kraus consolidation
items.quote: Currently the gross margins have gone down because of the change in the channel mix and the category mix.

items.statement: Average realisation per unit improved 14.4% YoY driven by lower discounting, not price hikes
items.quote: Average realisation per unit improved by 14.4% year-on-year, driven by higher full-price sales and increased share of Apparel in product mix.

items.statement: Accessories/others share rose to 12% from 8% due to Kraus categories like leggings, treggings, shorts
items.quote: It will be leggings, treggings, shorts.

items.statement: Management believes company is gaining market share based on B2B partner feedback
items.quote: Looking at the scenarios or maybe to the B2B partners, I think I will be on the gaining side that I will be gaining some percentage of market share.

items.statement: Growth funded through internal accruals; no incremental debt needed unless inorganic opportunity arises
items.quote: Right now our growth can be achieved through internal accruals. So I don't think there is a need for an increment of the debt. However, if there is any opportunity for an inorganic growth, maybe we may look into it.

items.statement: Exports ~3-4% of revenue; no strategy to expand exports significantly
items.quote: Our export is not very big because we are not doing any labels. We are doing our own brands only. So around 3% to 4% will be there. And this year also it will be the same.

items.statement: No price hikes planned for next quarter due to tough competitive market
items.quote: No, we are not taking any price hikes for the next quarter. Because you know the market is very tough and competitive. So, you cannot talk about any price hike overnight.

items.statement: Lawman and Integriti re-strategised; growth expected from H2 FY26
items.quote: We have re-strategised it, re-positioned it, okay. We should feel -- we feel that, okay, the growth for them should start coming from the second half of this year.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue guidance of INR 1,500 crores for FY26 with upside potential to be confirmed next quarter; margins maintained at current levels plus/minus 0.5%
items.quote: General guidance, as mentioned earlier, I still stick to INR 1,500 crores for this financial year with a certain upside potential and which will be confirmed in the next quarter, and margins will be maintained at the current levels plus/minus 0.5%.

items.statement: Expects to exceed current guidance of INR 15 billion consol for FY26 and INR 18 billion consol for FY27 based on strong order flow and OEM forecasts
items.quote: Currently, we have given a guidance of INR 15 billion consol for this year and INR 18 billion consol for next year. Looking at the way that the orders are flowing in and the forecast given by our OEMs, we will exceed these guidances.

items.statement: Standalone manufacturing order book at INR 14.68 billion: INR 10.8 billion generator & motor, INR 3.48 billion railways, INR 0.11 billion spares & aftermarket, INR 0.29 billion Turkey
items.quote: Order book for the manufacturing segment is INR 14.68 billion, out of which INR 10.8 billion is our generator and motor business, INR 3.48 billion is railways, spares and aftermarket business INR 0.11 billion, and INR 0.29 billion is the Turkey business.

items.statement: Q1 order inflow INR 3.92 billion, up 32% YoY; exports and deemed exports INR 2.57 billion (66% of inflow)
items.quote: Order inflow during the quarter is INR 3.92 billion, an increase of 32% on a year-on-year basis. Order inflow from exports and deemed exports is INR 2.57 billion, compared to INR 2.14 billion previous year. 66% of our quarterly order inflow is from exports.

items.statement: Executable order book for FY26 at INR 1,450 crores, providing comfort for INR 1,500 crore revenue guidance
items.quote: We have executable order for this year, INR 1,450 crores. And as Nikhil said, there is an upward revenue possible, but we have given an indication of INR 1,500 crores. So, book and bill looks to be only INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 18.7% in Q1 FY26 vs 17.17% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is 18.7%, including other income, excluding exceptionals and treasury income versus 17.17% over the same period previous year.

items.statement: FY26 capex plan INR 40-45 crores: INR 20 crores replacement (equal to depreciation), rest for growth
items.quote: Yes. See, replacement is around INR 20 crores, which is equal to the depreciation amount and the other is for the growth.

items.statement: Third plant progressive commissioning in Q2 and Q3 FY26; current facility potential INR 2,000 crores, optimizable to INR 2,300-2,400 crores without major new investment for next two years
items.quote: Initially, we will have an additional capacity to take us to around INR 2,000 crores, but we are already working on optimization and better manufacturing, lean manufacturing and other things like that. So, we easily see a potential to take this to INR 2,300-2,400 crores.

items.statement: US imposed additional 25% tariffs (total 50%) on Indian imports; company activating Plan B to shift 4-5% of sales (direct US exports) to Turkey plant for 15% duty advantage
items.quote: I think we have reached that situation yesterday after the announcement of the additional 25% tariffs. And we will have to move part of our production to Turkey and do value addition over there to have the made in Turkey nameplate, which will then attract 15% duty, which is what Turkey has.

items.statement: 66% of Q1 order inflow from exports; US market ~15-20% of sales (75% via EU OEMs at 15% duty, 25% direct now facing 50% tariff)
items.quote: 66% of our quarterly order inflow is from exports. 34% is domestic.

items.statement: US and Europe demand forecasts for gas engine/turbine generators extremely high; even at 80% accuracy, expect to exceed guidance; data center/AI driving US, grid stabilization and renewables driving Europe
items.quote: Now coming to the market itself, the demand forecast from the US and Europe are extremely high for both gas engine and gas turbine generators, and we are expecting a big uptick of orders currently. Even if the forecast are 80% correct, we expect to exceed the guidance made for this year and next year.

items.statement: Steam turbine market (domestic + export) growing 10-12% steadily; strong pipeline for larger 4-pole machines in Q2; hydro segment excellent order inflow, next year among highest in company history
items.quote: Overall, we expect the steam turbine business for us, domestic plus export to grow around 10% to 12%. We're getting steam turbine orders from all over the world and demand is strong and steady.

items.statement: Motor business targeting INR 1.5 billion FY26, INR 2+ billion FY27; strong pipeline for synchronous and induction motors for export
items.quote: This year, we'll be still on track to achieve the targets what we have mentioned, which should be something like INR 1.5 billion. And next year, we're going to do INR 2-plus billion in the motor business.

items.statement: Railways business to supply US, Europe, Russia and India (Alstom) next FY; significant uptick expected
items.quote: Railways, we have orders now for the US market, for the European market and the Russian market. We'll be supplying to all these three markets next year. And of course, the Alstom order for India still continues. So next year, we'll be supplying to all the four markets and we'll see a significant uptick in our railway business in the next financial year.

items.statement: Working capital running at ~120 days due to high end-of-quarter billings; euro forwards booked for the year, well placed
items.quote: Working capital, actually, it is running around 120 days, and this is what it will be because the revenues are also towards the end of the quarter, there is very high billings and all, so it comes into the data. So 120 days is what you can estimate.

items.statement: Strong cash position of INR 2.3 billion maintained on consolidated basis
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong cash position of INR 2.3 billion.

items.statement: Turkey plant currently has 5-6 manufacturing staff; need only 5-10 more people for assembly/testing operations to handle redirected US orders
items.quote: We need some 5or 10 people. It's not a big deal. We don't need 500 people. We need maybe 10 people.

items.statement: No promoter selling planned for next 24-36 months
items.quote: There is nothing of that sort planned at least for the next two to three years. At this point of time, I can say that we are not at all looking at that for the next 24 months at least.

items.statement: Turkey operations carry currency risk if doing Turkish lira business; dollar/euro-based sales stable; geopolitical risk between India and Turkey not seen as trickling down to business
items.quote: So we have been there for seven years already in Turkey, and we have good experience in managing and operating our plant in that region. So if we are doing dollar or euro-based sales, the situation is quite stable. But the moment you start doing Turkish lira kind of a business, then it becomes from a currency point of view, unstable.

items.statement: UK design center started for 50-150 MW own-design generators; targeting commercialization FY28 onwards; leveraging existing manufacturing investment
items.quote: So, we are developing our own range of products for larger machines, say, 50 megawatt to 150 megawatt, our own design. And we need the design talent required to develop these products. The talent we have located in the UK and with UK nationals would like to work out of the UK.

items.statement: CO2 battery storage (Energy Dome) pilot commissioned in Italy; major Indian customer also entering this market; potential for hundreds of MW but too early to quantify; technology licensing expanding globally
items.quote: I don't know, it could enter into hundreds of megawatts after some time, but it's very, very hard for us to say today with just the pilot plants being commissioned, whether how quickly this technology is going to be absorbed and rolled out across the world.

items.statement: Trade receivables at INR 425 crores end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: Yes. It is INR 425 crores.

items.statement: Aftermarket/spares business ~6-7% of sales; growing via hydro refurbishment orders and export market participation (US exhibition); not expected to grow faster than product business
items.quote: So we said that our aftermarket business will be something like 6%, 7% of sales, and we'll stick to that.

items.statement: Expects 5-6% growth in FCL and 3-4% in LCL volumes in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We do not expect an increase of more than 5% to 6% in the full container load business and about 3% to 4% in LCL in this quarter.

items.statement: Plans 20% volume growth for Abhilaya last-mile delivery in FY26
items.quote: However, year -on-year, the volumes of Amazon go up, and we also plan to increase our volumes by about 20% in this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps to 3.0% in Q1 FY26 driven by operational efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA increased to ₹4.4 Cr from ₹1.4 Cr in Q1 FY25, with margins expanded by 200 basis points to 3 .0%, driven by operational efficiency improvements .

items.statement: Abhilaya subsidiary turned profitable with ₹13.34 lakhs net income in Q1 FY26
items.quote: A key highlight was the performance of sub sidiary One World Logistics Private Limited operating as Abhilaya, which turned profitable for the first time, posting a net income of ₹13.34 lakhs compared to losses in the prior year and preceding quarter.

items.statement: Expects Abhilaya profit to increase by ₹3-4 lakhs monthly from new Amazon warehouse contract
items.quote: This month, we have recently got a contract from Amazon for managing five of their warehouses. I do not know the actual revenue increase, but the profit will be at least three to four lakh rupees per month, additionally on this.

items.statement: LCL consolidation volumes reached 98,700+ CBMs in Q1 FY26 with 13% growth
items.quote: LCL consolidation volumes reached 98,700 plus CBMs, with imports of 40,456 CBMs and exports of 58,282 CBMs.

items.statement: Airfreight volumes improved to 368 tons in Q1 FY26 from 312 tons in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Airfreight volumes improved to 368 tons in Q1 FY26 from 312 tons in Q1 FY25, supported by increased time-sensitive export shipments.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty causing exporters to hold back shipments, reducing freight levels
items.quote: The causes of the drop in volumes or dropping trade levels are mainly because of the uncertainty of the US tariffs.

items.statement: Freight levels directly impact margins - at $2,000/container can make $150, at $800 only $30-40
items.quote: Say, for example, on a full container load, if the freight level is $2,000, I can make up to $150. But when the freight level drops to $800, my margin comes down to maybe $30, $40.

items.statement: Fuel cost moves with freight levels - when freight goes up fuel cost goes up, when freight goes down fuel cost goes down
items.quote: When the freight level comes up, then the fuel cost increase is not a problem because we overall get the benefit of that. When the freight levels are high, our profitability is high, both for LCL and FCL business. When the freight levels go down, that time even the fuel cost also goes down.

items.statement: Cargo mix significantly affects profitability - concentrated volumes at preferred ports yield higher margins
items.quote: When there is a good cargo mix, for example, I get 55 cubic meters, and my overall volume is, say 10,000 cubic meters or say 20,000 cubic meters. But if I get 20,000 cubic meters to the ports where I want, my profitability will be high.

items.statement: Secured Amazon contract for managing five warehouses in last-mile delivery
items.quote: This month, we have recently got a contract from Amazon for managing five of their warehouses.

items.statement: Targeting freight forwarders, custom house agents and global MNCs for LCL/FCL business
items.quote: We have a very aggressive sales team and we are also tapping the freight forwarders or the custom house clearing agents who are our customers and we also offer our services to some of the global MNCs for the LCL and for the FCL.

items.statement: Investing in automation, digital platforms and supply chain visibility across LCL, FCL, Airfreight and last-mile
items.quote: The company continued strengthening capabilities across LCL, FCL, Airfreight and last-mile delivery through investments in automation, digital platforms, and enhanced supply chain visibility.

items.statement: Consolidating last-mile delivery centers to increase density rather than adding new centers
items.quote: Going further, at this point of time, we do not plan to increase the number of centres that do the delivery. We are consolidating our position to ensure that we get more dense deliveries.

items.statement: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy improving efficiency and expanding capacity
items.quote: Government initiatives such as PM Gati shakti and the National Logistics Policy, along with sustained investment in road, rail and port connectivity, are improving efficiency and expanding capacity.

items.statement: Does not expect freight levels to rise in next six months due to global tariff uncertainty
items.quote: We do not expect the freight levels to go up , at least in the next six month s. But I at least expect that at least steady freight levels will help us to at least plan something.

items.statement: India logistics sector expected to grow 8-10% annually driven by express parcels, 3PL and cold chain
items.quote: Looking ahead, the sector is expected to grow at 8% to 10% annually, driven by express parcels, integrated 3PL and cold chain services, with strong fundamentals and supportive policies positioning India's logistics industry for continuous expansion.

items.statement: Revamped department, trained staff and deployed bots to improve operational efficiency
items.quote: We have revamped our department, we have trained our people to extend. We are also using bots wherever possible. And because of tha t, the efficiency has gone up , and that is being seen in the increase in profitability.

items.statement: Guided 800 COCO store openings in FY26, on track to achieve target
items.quote: Just to clarify we had earlier guided 800 stores not 900, and we remain on track. As of now, we're aligned with the 800-store mark, and we're confident of reaching close to 800 stores within this financial year.

items.statement: Guided 150-200 FOFO store openings in FY26
items.quote: Nearly 150 to 200 stores in current time.

items.statement: Expect overall business to turn strongly profitable in 12-18 months as 600-700 stores reach maturity
items.quote: For us to see a meaningful shift in profitabil ity, we believe around 600 to 700 stores need to enter that mature bracket say, 18 to 36 months old. Once that happens, the economics will change significantly, and we expect the business to turn strongly profitable. We estimate this transition will take another 12 to 18 months

items.statement: Store-level breakeven at INR 2-2.2 lakhs monthly GMV with INR 1.2 lakhs monthly expenses
items.quote: So, all together it is INR1.2 lakhs per month per store expense. And in COCO store, we have a handsome 60% gross margin. So, roughly at INR 2 to 2.2 lakhs revenue, the store comes near to breakeven.

items.statement: DavaIndia network expanded to 1,745 stores (986 COCO, 759 FOFO) as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: Our DavaIndia store network expanded to 1,745 stores nationwide as on 31 June 2025, comprising 986 COCO and 759 FOFO outlets.

items.statement: Added 163 new stores in Q1 FY26 (134 COCO, 29 FOFO)
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 163 new stores, including 134 COCO and 29 FOFO, reflecting our balanced approach of strengthening the company on infrastructure while advancing our Asset-light expansion model.

items.statement: Quarterly footfall more than doubled to 35.35 lakhs from 17.5 lakhs year-on-year
items.quote: This expansion drove a more than two-fold jump in quarterly footfall to INR35.35 lakhs versus INR17.5 lakhs last year, supported by heightened brand awareness and aggressive rollout.

items.statement: GMV grew 88% year-on-year to INR 87.78 crores
items.quote: The robust traffic translated into an 88% year-on-year GMV to INR87.78 crores, compared to INR46.58 crores in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.7% from loss in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA at INR4.83 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 4.7%.

items.statement: Mature COCO stores (36+ months) deliver ~30% store-level EBITDA margin; 24+ month stores at ~20%
items.quote: we currently have 29 stores that are over 36 months old, each generating an average GMV of INR6.56 lakhs per store per month. These stores deliver a store-level EBITDA margin of approximately 30%. In addition, we have 54 stores that have been operational for more than two years, and their store-level EBITDA margin is around 20%.

items.statement: Marketing expenses currently not more than 5% of total revenue, will moderately increase
items.quote: Currently, it is not more than 5% of total revenue.

items.statement: Nutra, OTC and ayurvedic contribute ~27% of revenue across store vintages
items.quote: So, what happens is that the nutra, the OTC and the ayurvedic all gives the equivalent push for the drug, which closely consumes to close to around the 27%.

items.statement: Conversion rate over 90-95% as most patients visiting are aware of generic availability
items.quote: Since this is a generic pharmacy, most patients visiting the store are already aware that they'll find generic medicines here. As a result, the conversion rate is exceptionally high. For instance, if the daily footfall is around 20 customers, nearly 19 of them end up making a purchase. This translates to a conversion ratio of over 90-95%.

items.statement: 80% repeat customer rate confirmed
items.quote: Yes. Absolutely, right!

items.statement: Mature store (36+ months) average monthly GMV INR 6.56 lakhs; 9-12 month stores at INR 2.05 lakhs
items.quote: we currently have 29 stores that are over 36 months old, each generating an average GMV of INR6.56 lakhs per store per month.

items.statement: Store maturation trajectory: Year 1 INR 2-2.25L, Year 2 INR 3-3.5L, Year 3 INR 4.5L, Year 4 INR 6L monthly GMV
items.quote: Typically, a store in its first year achieves monthly sales of around INR 2 to INR2.25 lakhs. In the second year, this increases to INR 3 to INR 3.5 lakhs. By the third year, stores reach INR4.5 lakhs per month, and in the fourth year, they go up to INR 6 lakhs per month per store.

items.statement: 9-12 month vintage stores (136 stores) at INR 2.05L monthly GMV, expected to reach breakeven INR 2.4L next quarter
items.quote: These stores are now averaging INR 2,05,000 in monthly GMV. Based on their growth trajectory, we expect them to reach breakeven INR 2,40,000 per store per month in the next quarter.

items.statement: Hyperlocal B2C model complies with state-level online pharmacy regulations
items.quote: Now, you see the regulations of the way how it's been drafted for the online business for India. It is more so to ensure that we deliver in the respective state and similar. So, our hyper local model would ensure that it not only enhances, builds efficient supply chain and robust management, but it would also increase the speed.

items.statement: DavaIndia is India's only 100% private-label generic pharmacy chain; Jan Aushadhi is government-backed competitor
items.quote: So apart from the government, there are no purely generic pharmacies in India at this level. The rest of the companies also provide branded along with generic. There are many such small companies. But purely in the generic space, Jan Aushadhi backed by Government, and apart from this, DavaIndia is the only player in 100% Private label Generic medicine in India.

items.statement: Appointed Suniel Shetty as brand ambassador; plan TV commercial and advertising campaign
items.quote: To further strengthen visibility and connect with consumers, we appointed a renewed actor and entrepreneur, Mr. Suniel Shetty, as our brand ambassador during this quarter.

items.statement: May potentially pause growth if environmental factors or unforeseen situations arise
items.quote: We are not really planning to slow down unless there are some environmental factors or unforeseen situation that comes in, which you and me don't know at this point of time.

items.statement: B2C hyperlocal delivery app launched PAN India on Android and iOS
items.quote: The platform is now launched. The B2C portal is what it is. It is also in the form of an app, both in Android and the iOS. It is available and it is full through.
