items.quote: So far, we've closed a total of 19 stores. Out of these, 6 have been relocated to better-performing locations, while the remaining 12 to 13 stores have been permanently shut down.

items.statement: FOFO store reductions in some states due to franchisee non-compliance with terms
items.quote: So, any franchisee who does not adhere to the terms and conditions of the organization does not fit on to stay as a franchisee. And we have to be careful and cognizant about the fact, and accordingly, the decisions are taken for that.

items.statement: 5,000 stores possible in next 2-3 years per management
items.quote: Okay. So, yes, it may be possible.

items.statement: Reaffirmed structural targets of RoE above 15% and RoA of 1% through the cycle
items.quote: Our ambition is not merely to grow, but to grow profitably and sustainably. We reaffirm our structural targets of RoE above 15% and RoA of 1% through the cycle.

items.statement: Expect credit expansion to outpace nominal GDP and industry growth driven by retail, government capex and green energy
items.quote: Looking ahead we expect credit expansion to outpace both nominal GDP and industry growth driven by calibrated exposure to consumption linked retail loans, government CapEx pipeline and green energy projects.

items.statement: Cost to income ratio effort to keep below 50% through the cycle
items.quote: While we still are sticking to our guidance that the cost to income ratio, our effort is to keep below 50. I am not giving any number whether it is 47, 45. The effort is through the cycle, we would like to maintain the cost to income ratio below 50.

items.statement: Recovery guidance of ₹7,000-8,000 crores from AUCA for FY26
items.quote: Recovery, yes, we had given a guidance of around ₹7,000 - 8,000 crores in recovery from AUCA, which means that ₹2,000 crores every quarter, but it is not uniformly distributed.

items.statement: Corporate credit growth target of 10-11% for FY26
items.quote: But as rightly said by the Chairman, that overall, we still think that we might have this year still a t around 10 -11% in corporate growth.

items.statement: Overall credit growth guidance of 12% for FY26 with potential upside to 13%
items.quote: That's the reason we are still sticking to 12%. And as the uncertainties get clea red, probably there is a potential upside of 13%.

items.statement: Total consolidated debt of INR6,826 crores as of June 30, 2025 with standalone debt at INR1,652 crores
items.quote: Total consolidated debt as on 30th June 2025 stood at INR6,826 crores. The stand-alone debt is at INR1,652 crores.

items.statement: Target to reduce standalone debt from INR1,650 crores to INR500-600 crores post monetization
items.quote: So we'll be basically addressing the INR1,650 crores of stand-alone debt, which will be brought to the typical levels of around, say, INR500 crores to INR600 crores max.

items.statement: Project level debt to reduce from INR6,800 crores to approximately INR1,000 crores including project loans post full monetization
items.quote: Yes, substantially lower than that, approximately in the range of, touch INR1,000 crores, including project loan.

items.statement: Monetization of 5 BOT and 5 HAM projects by September 30, 2025 expected to yield INR2,800-3,000 crores from BOT and INR1,100 crores from HAM
items.quote: The first 5 BOT, we are expecting around INR2,800 crores to INR3,000 crores, roughly INR3,000 crores. And balance of the 6 projects by June of around INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: HAM monetization: 5 projects by September, 4 by December, 2 by June 2026; total proceeds to fund SBI Macquarie exit of INR1,526 crores plus JN stake INR150 crores
items.quote: On the HAM side, for the first 5 set of projects, we expect the closure to happen by somewhere last week August or initial couple of weeks of September. So again, by September end definitely, these 5 projects also, closing will happen.

items.statement: BOT toll revenue grew 13% YoY to INR362 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26 in our BOT division, the company recorded a gross toll revenue of INR362 crores as against INR322 crores in Q1 FY '25, recording a growth of 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: Signed contract with Government of Guyana for Phase 2 East Bank-East Coast Road Linkage Project valued at USD 67 million with 18-month timeline
items.quote: On June 18, 2025, we signed and executed a contract with the government of Guyana Republic (Guyana’s Public Wo rks Department ) for Phase 2 of East Bank -East Coast Road Linkage Project. The project is valued at USD 67 million and comes with an 18-month execution time line

items.statement: Received LOA from Central Railway for Pachora-Jamner gauge conversion project worth INR568 crores including GST
items.quote: the Railway segment, we received LOA from Central Railway for an EPC project involving the gauge conversion from Pachora to Jamner in Maharashtra, covering approximately 53 kilometers. The scope of work includes earthworks, bridges, pathways, other civil works. This project valued at INR568 crores, including

items.statement: Secured INR1,387 crores contract from Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Department for intelligent traffic management across 5 circles
items.quote: ABL, along with its subsidiary, Ashoka Purestudy Technologies, secured contracts from Motor Vehicles Department, Maharashtra worth INR1,387 crores, including GST, to implement intelligent traffic management system across 5 major circles.

items.statement: NHAI changed bidding criteria reducing 20% of balance order book from net worth for eligibility calculation
items.quote: they have changed a little criteria for bidding with the reducing from the linking to the net worth and reducing 20% of your balance order book from the net worth and balance order net worth would only be considered for bidding

items.statement: Competition remains intense with 20-25 players in most NHAI EPC projects; new criteria may limit competition for larger HAM/BOT projects
items.quote: We have not seen any easing off. We see 20, 25 players in most of the projects. N ow they have changed a little criteria for bidding with the reducing from the linking to the net worth and reducing 20% of your balance order book from the net worth

items.statement: NHAI pipeline visibility of INR75,000 crores targeting INR1.5-1.8 lakh crores; states adding INR70,000 crores+ opportunities
items.quote: Currently, we have around INR75,000 crores is the visibility in the pipeline of NHAI and MoRTH, which they want to ramp up to around INR1.5 lakh crores to INR1.8 lakh crores.

items.statement: National toll revenue surged nearly 20% YoY to INR20,682 crores in Q1 with 1.17 billion vehicle trips; sector on track for INR80,000 crores in FY26
items.quote: Toll revenue surged nearly 20% year-on-year to INR20,682 crores in Q1 with 1.17 billion vehicle trips recorded during the period. The sustained rise in vehicle movement coupled with revised toll rate positions the sector on track to exceed around INR80,000 crores in toll revenues for FY '26.

items.statement: Green hydrogen MOU with Bihar government has seen no further development
items.quote: So there is no further development in this. We've signed an MOU, but there's no further development.

items.statement: Monetization proceeds of INR1,200 crores net of SBI Macquarie exit to be used initially for working capital debt reduction
items.quote: This will be largely utilized for initially reducing our working capital debt. And then future plans will be taken up post September.

items.statement: Acuite Ratings reaffirmed long-term rating at AA and short-term at A1+ as of June 3, 2025
items.quote: Acuite Ratings & Research reaffirmed our ratings for long-term bank facilities at AA and short term at A1+ as of June 3, 2025.

items.statement: Revenue mix Q1 FY26: Road EPC 52.4%, Road HAM 11.6%, Power T&D 19.7%, Railways 6.7%, Buildings/Others 19.6%
items.quote: Our revenue contribution for each segment for Q1 FY '26 is Road EPC contributed 52.4%, Road HAM contributed 11.6%, Power T&D contributed 19.7%, Railways stood at 6.7% and other segments like Building EPC and Others contributed 19.6%.

items.statement: Full-year revenue guidance of INR 2,250 crores maintained; expects to achieve or surpass full-year EBITDA margin guidance of 16.5%-17.5%
items.quote: We guided for INR 2,250 crores. We did INR2,400 crores last year. I have maintained that quarter-on-quarter should not be compared for a construction company. Whatever full year guidance from EBITDA, PAT, cash PAT, top line was given has been achieved.

items.statement: Order inflow target for FY26 is INR 4,000-4,500 crores; expects to surpass this target
items.quote: So we have already given a target for the current full year, which is about INR 4,000 crores to INR4,500 crores. And we do believe that we should be able to surpass that, number one.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is INR 75-80 crores; Q1 capex was INR 34.03 crores
items.quote: The capex in the Q1 has been INR34.03 crores. And the full year, we look to this -- in the current financial year, go to approximately INR75 crores to INR80 crores.

items.statement: Order book exceeds INR 11,000 crores excluding MHADA order; provides 3+ years visibility
items.quote: And when we speak to you about optimism and our targets, obviously, we are talking about on the basis of the existing order book, which is in excess of INR11,000 crores, excluding the MHADA order, which has to be added, which means you have a visibility of 3 years or more very clearly.

items.statement: CIDCO target: INR 700-800 crores for remaining period; MHADA subcontract: INR 350 crores; NBCC target: INR 60 crores/month from October
items.value: INR 700-800 crores (CIDCO), INR 350 crores (MHADA), INR 60 crores/month (NBCC)
items.quote: We are committed to give more than INR 700 crores to INR800 crores in CIDCO for the remaining period, all right? We are committed to do about INR350 crores as a subcontract that is in the books of Capacit'e Infraprojects Limited in MHADA. And obviously, we have to go to an average billing cycle of INR 60 crores from October onwards in NBCC.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on demand; selective bidding for quality clients with premium pricing; strong bid pipeline with pick-and-choose approach
items.quote: So after all of us having seen COVID, and the NBFC crisis in 2018, '19, while we are optimistic, but we are cautiously optimistic. So we will continue to work for only those clients which sui t our requirements, are ready to give that little bit of premium in exchange of quality construction to be done on time

items.statement: Projects 90-95% manned; using eFORCE app for productivity tracking and LRD for recruitment; labor shortage limits potential growth to 30-35%
items.quote: At the moment, we are close to 90%, 95% of labor requirement across our project sites. We have adopted very innovative ways of recruiting workmen, improving -- further improving their work conditions, adding lunch, dinners, breakfast to their -- as amenities is being provided to them.

items.statement: No change in margins or payment terms for new orders vs FY25; avoids orders with inferior terms after NBFC/COVID experience
items.quote: No change. If the payment terms are not better, we would like to remain away from those orders. Every quarter, I have sai d and I reiterate that the quality of clients and the commercial terms cannot

items.statement: Ex-retention working capital days stable at 172.44 days; Q1 collections INR 543 crores vs INR 599 crores revenue; total collections now INR 756 crores; expects substantial positive cash flow improvement in FY26
items.quote: The working capital, which was on -- excluding retention, 172.44 days as on 31st March '25 has not increased in quarter 1. The total collections in quarter 1 as against the revenue of INR 599 crores stood at INR543 crores which is a significant improvement.

items.statement: Cash credit interest down to 10.3%; NCDs at 13%+ reduced to INR 61 crores from INR 100 crores; targets average interest below 10%; absolute finance cost to be lower in FY26
items.quote: So the working -- see, cash credit limits, interest have come down to 10.3%. We see further improvement over the -- getting into the next quarter. That's number one. The non-convertible debentures, which we had taken from certain -- which is high interest-bearing, upward of 13% is only about INR61 crores as against INR100 crores outstanding.

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduction underway: Avendus pledge reduced by 10 lakh shares; aims to eliminate all pledges except SBI CIDCO project-specific pledge by FY26 end
items.quote: Apart from there, there was a pledge of shares with Avendus, which has reduced by INR5 lakhs -- 10 lakh shares, I'm sorry. And we believe that this reduction will be much more aggressive over the next 2 quarters. We do believe that by the end of the current financial year, there will not be any pledge with any other entity except State Bank of India for the project-specific limit of CIDCO.

items.statement: Q1 revenue INR 599 crores; average monthly run rate ~INR 200 crores; targets improvement in Q2 and substantial improvement from Q3
items.quote: Since we have done INR599 crores, the average is close to INR 200 crores, which we seek to improve in quarter 2 and improve substantially starting quarter 3.

items.statement: Signature Global Phase 1 profit recognition started; NBCC profit recognition to start Q2; Tata JV profits similar to FY25, momentum increasing from FY27
items.quote: Signature Global is in 2 phases. So Phase 1 under execution, we have started recognizing profit because the threshold has been crossed. As far as NBCC is concerned, we should start recognizing profit from quarter 2 onwards, that is the current quarter.

items.statement: Labor shortage is a major industry-wide challenge limiting growth potential; driven by Middle East and Eastern Europe demand; growth targets factor this constraint
items.quote: Had this challenge not been there, we would be discussing growth of 30%, 35%, if not more. But this challenge is there because t here is a huge demand from Middle East. There's also demand coming in from Eastern

items.statement: Added Hinduja Group UK to portfolio; negotiating new private sector orders with existing clients; government bidding for IIT, NBCC projects
items.quote: We have added Hinduja Group of UK to our portfolio already. And we do believe that over the next month or so, we should be in a position to announce a few projects with our existing clients in the private sector.

items.statement: Focus on mixed-use projects in Mumbai; healthcare and data center opportunities; avoids shell-only data center work without electromechanical scope
items.quote: I do believe that we will add something in health care. We will add -- most of it will come from mixed use. Because you see there is a remarkable shift in Mumbai, where you are seeing a lot of mixed use construction happening in South Mumbai as well.

items.statement: Monsoon losses factored at 15-21 days in Mumbai; winter NGT stoppages 10-15 days in North India; early monsoon onset in May 2025 was unexpected
items.quote: You see that the revenue targets are given for the full year, taking into consideration the heavy monsoons for over 2 to 2.5 months in Mumbai, where ideally generally on our experience, you lose 15 to 21 days every year. Similarly, during winters, you lose 10 to 15 days due to NGT and the stoppages in Northern India, including NCR.

items.statement: EY audit flagged INR 66 crores recoverable trade receivables; company holds properties worth >INR 100 crores as coverage
items.quote: EY in quarter 4, which was their last quarter audit for financial year '24, '25 have mentioned INR 66 crores, but also have mentioned along with that, the properties available with the company to cover this INR66 crores, which are in excess of INR100 crores.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target Rs 1,000 crore with EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: The revenue target what we have fixed is Rs . 1,000 crores for FY25-26 with a margin between 18%-20%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth 15-20% with EBITDA margin 18-20%
items.quote: Even for the next year we are envisaging a growth of about 15 % to 20% in our revenue and EBITDA margins again we would like to keep between 18% to 20%.

items.statement: FY26 capex Rs 116 crore (Rs 52 crore existing site, Rs 64 crore Hamirpur)
items.quote: We have earmarked a capital expenditure of approximately Rs. 116 crores for this year, Rs. 52 crores for the existing site and Rs. 64 crores for some Hamirpur site.

items.statement: Hamirpur site total investment ~Rs 400-500 crore to reach Rs 1,000-1,100 crore revenue in 3-4 years
items.quote: We have already spent almost Rs. 50 crores there and 54 now is going on and we need to invest almost about Rs. 400 crores roughly. Satya Prakash Gupta: Asset turnover are 2-2.5, so 400 crores to 500 crores of investment will be required

items.statement: PEDA capacity expanded from 2,000 to 6,000 tpa, further to 8,500 tpa by Q2 FY26
items.quote: commissioned the expanded PEDA Intermediate Facility, increasing the capacity from 2 ,000 tons to 6 ,000 tons per annum with a further scale -up to 8,500 metric tons per annum on track for Q2 FY 26.

items.statement: Formulation capacity augmented by 3,500 tpa
items.quote: Successfully commissioned the expansion of our formulation plant, adding 3,500 metric tons per annum of capacity.

items.statement: Current blended capacity utilization ~80% (technical 73%, formulation fully utilized)
items.quote: Current capacity utilization is around 80% on blended basis. Technical will be around 73% and formulation is fully utilized.

items.statement: Global agrochemical market showing early recovery; inventory normalized; raw material prices stable
items.quote: The global agrochemical market is showing early signs of recovery, driven by a revival in demand and gradual improvement in prices. Inve ntory levels across distribution channels have largely normalized and raw material prices remain stable

items.statement: Focus on value over volume; premiumization and better product mix driving margin improvement
items.quote: We continue our focus on innovation and premiumization yielded positive results, driving an improvement in gross margins. We con stantly prioritized value over volume, reflecting our long -term strategy of sustainable, profitable growth.

items.statement: Export order book better YoY; good orders for Prosulfocarb, Folpet, Captan
items.quote: Export order book is also growing, sir. That is true, when compared to last year our export order book is relatively much better. We have orders for our major products like Prosulfocarb as well as for Folpet as well as for Captan we have got very good export orders.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Pretilachlor normalized prices; previously losing money, now reasonable margin
items.quote: with this anti-dumping duty, the prices have slightly normalized. Otherwise last year we were losing money on Pretilachlor but now we are getting a reasonable margin in this.

items.statement: Competitive with China on major molecules; anti-dumping duty levels playing field for Pretilachlor
items.quote: We have optimized our products and we are competitive to China now and we are able to compete with them. There is no problem at all. And in some products, for example in Pretilachlor because of this anti -dumping duty, now we are at a better playing field.

items.statement: High herbicide inventory in Q4 FY25 liquidated; working capital limits low; interest cost to reduce
items.quote: We have borrowing since Q4 FY25 have accumulated a large inventory of our herbicide . N ow they have been liquidated and we are receiving payments. So, now our working capital limit, they are at a very low level. So, interest cost will be reduced in subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Capex funded primarily from internal accruals; strong balance sheet with good free cash flow
items.quote: India Pesticides Ltd. has its strong balance sheet with the ability to generate good free cash flow. Company is planning to fuel its Capex plan primarily with internal accruals.

items.statement: New product launches: 2 in IPL, 3 in Shalvis lined up for FY27
items.quote: For the year 2026 and onwards, number of product launches are in pipeline. There are two products in IPL and three products in Shalvis are lined up for launches next year.

items.statement: All major Indian agrochemical companies source key molecules from IPL; Rallis, UPL among customers
items.quote: India Pesticides Ltd. is increasingly recognized as a trusted partner by both domestic and global players, with all major Indian companies sourcing one or more key molecules from us.

items.statement: China remains a challenge but IPL competitive on major molecules; no threat in core products
items.quote: China is always a challenge, sir. Dheeraj Kumar Jain: We have optimized our products and we are competitive to China now and we are able to compete with them. There is no problem at all

items.statement: ADS revenue target for FY26 is INR 280-300 crores
items.quote: we would want to double our revenue from the past year and try and reach about INR 280 crores to INR 300 crores. This is what I have indicated in the previous con call. And we are on a path to reach that.

items.statement: Sweden business expected to grow 20%+ in FY26 with double-digit margins
items.quote: overall, if you look at full year, we should be achieving a 20% plus growth in Sweden business on a full year basis. The margin profile will also be substantially better than what we had last year, and this is basically on back of a host of factors, including the volume increases, the better capacity utilization, and some automation that we are currently in the process of implementing, which will

items.statement: Sweden business expected to stabilize from Q3 FY26 at similar levels
items.quote: We expect this momentum to stabilize from quarter 3 of FY '26 and remain at similar levels thereafter.

items.statement: Order book at INR 20,243 million as of June 2025 with 60%+ international orders
items.quote: As of June 2025, our order book stood at INR 20,243 million with more than 60% of orders coming from the international orders.

items.statement: Added INR 1,732 million new orders in Q1 FY26, led by ADS, xEV, tech agnostic, ICE
items.quote: We added INR1,732 million worth of new orders during the quarter, mainly from the ADS segment, followed by the xEV and tech agnostic, and lastly, ICE orders.

items.statement: ADS order book near INR 750 crores, targeting INR 1,000 crores in 3 years
items.quote: Like last time, I have said that in 3 years' time, we are looking at about reaching INR 1,000 crores. And we are already about -- including our current business that we are executing and the new order book, we are around INR 750 crores, close to about INR 750 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.2%, up 10 bps YoY and 90 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 1,321 million with a margin -- at a margin of 17.2%, which is a growth of 10 basis points on a year-on-year basis and sequentially about 90 basis points.

items.statement: Targeting 20% EBITDA margin mid to long term, 50-75 bps annual improvement when normalized
items.quote: Yes. Actually, this 20% is a mid to long-term target that we are working on. Of course, the change in product portfolio to more of 20% coming from non-automotive, 20% from xEV and that too -- and also stabilization of our MMRFIC would definitely aid the path towards 50%. I would say that while we were fortunate to maintain our margins at this, we were -- unfortunately, there are so many headwinds

items.statement: Domestic 2-wheeler scooters declined, motorcycles above 200cc and entry-level bikes strong
items.quote: The primary impact was due to a decline in 2 -wheeler scooter sales, whereas 2 -wheeler motorcycles category continues to thrive and deliver positive performance. We witnessed, like the industry, strong rural demand for the entry-level bikes and healthy urba n demand for the premium motorcycles, which are above 200 cc

items.statement: Exports from India excluding ADS declined 20.6% due to global uncertainties
items.quote: Exports from India, excluding ADS, declined by 20.6% due to global uncertainties.

items.statement: US exports slowdown impacted PV, xEV, non-auto; ADS and premium 2-wheeler motorcycles resilient
items.quote: Most segments were impacted by the slowdown in the US exports, particularly the passenger vehicles, xEVs and non-auto categories. However, ADS and premium 2-wheeler motorcycles continued to demonstrate resilience.

items.statement: Sweden automation investments to complete by end of Q2 FY26 for cost optimization
items.quote: by the end of Q2, we would also expect our automation to be fully in place, which means there is further cost optimization that can happen.

items.statement: Aluminum forging capacity expanded with 2,500 and 4,000 tonne presses at Bidadi
items.quote: we have added 2,500 and 4,000 Tonne presses into our new forge shop in Bidadi, which would also be catering and we are looking at some very, very intricate new components to be developed.

items.statement: Sweden plant capacity utilization improving, automation to stabilize by end of Q2
items.quote: On the operational side, we have been -- we have invested. We are in the process of investing. Over the next 2 to 3 months' time, we'll stabilize and conclude those investment part of it to reap the benefits of this growth.

items.statement: ADS segment growing with high value-added aerospace and semiconductor components
items.quote: Unlike the earlier times, now because of our track record and also that our focus on high value-added components, we have actually added a lot of capability in terms of taking our product sizes up to 4 meters on Y axis, along with very, very intricate special capability on machining. So these are resulting in high value-added components today compared to what we were getting earlier where the numb

items.statement: New orders from semicon customer, US tractor manufacturer, North American EV maker, Israeli defense
items.quote: our largest order was from our semicon customer. Then from -- also, we have got one new customer added, which is from a US -based tractor manufacturer. Then we have from our regular Aerospace, who have been our customer for a long time, we have received orders from them as well. Of course, we have got further orders from our largest EV manufacturer based out of North America. So it's been a mix of

items.statement: USMCA regional value content requirement at 65%, may rise to 75-80%, driving localization needs
items.quote: the more concern, what we understood was on -- RVC, which is residual value content, which is currently I think is at 65% on the USMCA region, which means that all the value addition that they expect on a vehicle level to achieve 65% from the USMCA region. That seems to be more focused because they expect that to go up, and there are indications that it might be kind of looking at between 75% and

items.statement: Europe business grew 3.5% YoY, Sweden up 80% on low base, other countries up 11%
items.quote: However, our Europe business grew by about 3.5%. This was primarily due to our Swedish business, which grew by over 80% on a year-on-year basis because of the low base effect of Sweden. And revenues from other countries delivered a healthy growth of 11%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow net of tax INR 962 million, 13% of operating revenue
items.quote: Our operating cash flow net of tax continues to be healthy and stood at INR 962 million, which is 13% of the operating revenue.

items.statement: Net interest cost INR 36 million in Q1 FY26, significantly lower than previous year
items.quote: On a net basis, we also booked some interest income during the quarter. Net basis, we had an interest cost of about INR 36 million, which is significantly lower than the previous year.

items.statement: Aluminum forging revenue target INR 500 crores by FY27
items.quote: If you really look at our order book and the way that we should target about INR 500 crores coming out of overall aluminum portfolio.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty may cause supply chain realignment, impacting FY28 revenue assumptions
items.quote: if there is some realignment of supply chain that would happen in the future, if this tariff impact is going to continue or worsen, then we are looking at realigning our business models. So it could have an impact on the overall pricing.

items.statement: IHCL invests INR204 crores for 51% stake in ANK and Pride (Clarks Hotels and Resorts) with INR110 crores in ANK and INR94 crores in Pride
items.quote: This is a total investment of INR204 crores in the two companies, ANK and Pride, and the split is, as mentioned on the slide, INR110 crores into ANK and INR94 crores in Pride.

items.statement: Enterprise value of the transaction is INR240 crores with INR160 crores primary investment and INR44 crores secondary
items.quote: If we do the math on that the enterprise value is about INR240 crores.

items.statement: 80% of INR204 crores investment is primary capital going into the companies for future growth including PIPs and management contract conversions
items.quote: Out of the INR204 crores, substantially almost 80% is primary investment and the balance is a small secondary investment in t he transaction, which means there is a large component sitting in the companies as capital for future growth

items.statement: Clarks portfolio adds 135 hotels (125 managed, 10 operating lease) with ~7,000 keys in 100+ locations, 70% in new geographies for Ginger
items.quote: Now what this does is it gets us 135 hotels under the Clarks brand, the majority of which will get repositioned and reimagined as Ginger hotels, totaling almost 7,000 keys in 100-plus locations.

items.statement: FY27 projected revenue INR60 crores with consolidated EBITDA INR20 crores; FY30 target revenue INR100 crores with consolidated EBITDA INR60 crores (INR20 crores fee + INR40 crores hotel EBITDA)
items.quote: FY '27 actually will be the first full year of sort of once the transaction is closed. And we think we can actually get closer to INR60 crores of revenues in that year and will result in overall margins coming closer to 30% on EBITDA and in IHCL consolidated EBITDA, which includes the fee we will earn from the hotels to close to INR20 crores.

items.statement: Upside from management contract to revenue share conversions estimated at INR50-75 crores revenue (7-8 hotels at INR6-8 crores each) not included in projections
items.quote: Additionally, this does not capture any upside from management contracts shifting to revenue share, which could actually be close to INR50 crores to INR75 crores, which we think is a conservative number, per hotel, typically INR6 crores to INR8 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Ginger Lean Luxe hotels achieve 50%+ EBITDA margins; Clarks portfolio targeted to reach 50% EBITDA margin by FY30 after transition
items.quote: One was obviously the strong growth, but also the fact that most of the hotels, which have actually moved to Lean Luxe as a portfolio have a margin close to 50% plus on EBITDA.

items.statement: Mid-scale segment fastest growing in India from 40% of branded supply in 2014 to 43% in 2024, expected to reach ~50% by 2030 driven by population growth
items.quote: We also know that the mid-scale segment in India is fastest growing from 2014, when there was 100,000 branded rooms, the lower end was almost 40% of the total supply. 10 years later, that number went to 43. And we think that in another 5 to 6 years by 2030, this segment or this market share of this segment will definitely be closer to 50% or so.

items.statement: Ginger portfolio to cross 300+ hotels in next 18 months from current ~250, becoming market leader in mid-scale segment in 12-18 months
items.quote: And as we continue our growth journey, this almost 250 hotels portfolio should cross 300-plus easily over the next 18 months or so.

items.statement: 85-90% of Clarks portfolio to be repositioned as Ginger, remainder as Gateway or Selection brands based on asset positioning
items.quote: We do believe that the majority -- significant majority, anything between 85% to 90% for Ginger is fine. The rest we will take a call during this period of completion of the deal and find the best value proposition.

items.statement: Brij Hospitality adds 19 hotels (10 operational with 360-380 keys, 9 in pipeline) with sales and distribution agreement signed
items.quote: The Brij has 19 hotels, of which 10 are in operation, totaling around 360-380 keys. And of this 10 in operation, there is another 9 in pipeline.

items.statement: Ginger brand targets 1,000 hotels potential; Accelerate 2030 strategy targets 700 hotels portfolio by 2030, currently at ~530-550 post-acquisition
items.quote: The potential for Ginger brand or the mid-scale brand for the company is 1,000 Gingers. You cannot get there organically. It will just take too long.

items.statement: Clarks promoter group (three young cousins/brothers) to continue driving growth and management with IHCL governance support and select IHCL personnel
items.quote: The job done by these three young cousins and brothers was so phenomenal in making 150 hotels that, that is one of the reasons we have integrated them in the journey forward. So they will continue to drive growth and management.

items.statement: Procurement strength to grow significantly with addition of 7,000 keys; shared services (accounting, controlling, back-of-house, IT) to create cost synergies
items.quote: very importantly, our procurement strength will grow by leaps and bound. I think addition of such significant number of hotels should help Indian Hotels Company Limited in general and Ginger brand, in particular, in getting synergies in procure ment, synergies in shared

items.statement: Management contract to revenue share conversions not guaranteed; require hotel-by-hotel discussions and owner support; not included in base projections
items.quote: It's not straightforward. And that's why if you see our projections, which we gave out, we haven't really included that portion. We have just t alked about this as a potential upside

items.statement: No plan to acquire remaining 49% stake in ANK and Pride; strategic partnership with promoters continuing to drive business
items.quote: As far as the 49% goes, there is no plan as of now to purchase the 49%. We are, like I said, entering into a strategic partnership. And this is not because they are pure financial investors, they're also going to be driving the business.

items.statement: Primary capital (INR160 crores) to fund property improvement plans, management contract conversions (INR2-5 crores per hotel), and potential Ginger Big Box model replication
items.quote: Essentially, this is obviously a conversation to be had once the transaction closes. But the idea is to see how can we use this capital, which is available at disposal to bring most or if not all the hotels onto the Ginger platform as quickly as possible.

items.statement: FY27 transition year with INR10 crores EBITDA after fees; FY28 expected to show full trajectory upliftment on EBITDAR and EBITDA margins
items.quote: But even if you look at FY '27, there is actually a trajectory for upliftment on EBITDAR margin and then consequentl y on EBITDA itself. items.statement: FY25 interim dividend INR 5 (two tranches of INR 2.5); final dividend INR 3.35 recommended; total INR 8.35 (~42% of profit)
items.quote: For FY25 NTPC has paid interim dividend of INR 5, and this was in the two tranches of INR 2.5 each and further Board of Directors have recommended final dividend of INR 3.35 subject to the shareholders' approval in the upcoming AGM. With this, the total dividend will become INR 8.35 which is approximately 42% of our profit.

items.statement: Captive coal production 46 MT in FY25 (28% YoY growth); target 50 MT in FY26; aim to meet 25% coal requirement from captive mines by FY30
items.quote: In FY25, the company achieved a production milestone of 46 million tons, reflecting a strong 28% year-on-year growth and underscoring its operational excellence in mining. Looking ahead, NTPC targets meeting at least 25% of its coal requirement through captive mining by FY30, further enhancing fuel security and supply reliability.

items.quote: So, there are some estimates as of now that it will be somewhere between INR 15 crore to INR 20 crore per megawatt. If that is going to be the cost, tariff will be in the range of anywhere between INR 6 to INR 8.

items.statement: FGD investment on existing plants is cost-plus and will be compensated; new projects FGD on hold pending CEA committee review
items.quote: For the old projects, already the cost is taken care. It is cost plus only. For the new projects, following the guideline, we have kept the FGD on hold. In the meantime, CEA has formed a committee to decide upon the financial and all. Of course, we will be in advantage because we have done the FGD. We will be compensated.
